## Deployment Verification Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh render <nova\|buster> [image\|code]` | Render the selected release without applying it; image is the default mode. Requires the selected runtime release. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh buildkit-preflight [image] [pull-secret]` | Check rootless BuildKit with a temporary cluster Pod; image defaults to BUILDKIT_ROOTLESS_PREFLIGHT_IMAGE and must be digest-pinned. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh buster-buildkit-smoke` | Deprecated alias for nova-buildkit-preflight. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh nova-kubernetes-fixture-preflight [image] [secret-name]` | Exercise a retained Kubernetes fixture; image falls back to KUBECLAW_KUBERNETES_PREFLIGHT_IMAGE; Secret to KUBECLAW_KUBERNETES_PREFLIGHT_SECRET then kubeclaw-fixture-preflight. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh nova-http-preflight [image]` | Exercise the real HTTP provider path through Nova and Buster; select a digest-pinned workload image or its command-specific environment input. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh nova-a11y-preflight [image]` | Exercise the real browser accessibility provider path through Nova and Buster; select a digest-pinned workload image or its command-specific environment input. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh nova-api-preflight [image]` | Exercise the real API provider path through Nova and Buster; select a digest-pinned workload image or its command-specific environment input. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh nova-lighthouse-preflight [image]` | Exercise the real Lighthouse provider path through Nova and Buster; select a digest-pinned workload image or its command-specific environment input. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh nova-visual-preflight [image]` | Exercise the real visual comparison provider path through Nova and Buster; select a digest-pinned workload image or its command-specific environment input. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh nova-e2e-preflight [image]` | Exercise the real browser end-to-end provider path through Nova and Buster; select a digest-pinned workload image or its command-specific environment input. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh nova-security-preflight [image]` | Exercise the real security provider path through Nova and Buster; select a digest-pinned workload image or its command-specific environment input. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh nova-tailscale-preflight [image]` | Exercise the real Kubernetes/Tailscale provider path through Nova and Buster; select a digest-pinned workload image or its command-specific environment input. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh nova-production-preflights [image] [secret-name]` | Run production-required suite preflights; image falls back to KUBECLAW_PRODUCTION_PREFLIGHT_IMAGE; Secret to KUBECLAW_KUBERNETES_PREFLIGHT_SECRET then kubeclaw-fixture-preflight. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh buster-infra-smoke` | Publish through Redis and exercise deployed Buster, BuildKit and deployment. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh agent <nova\|buster> [--with-code]` | Deploy one agent; --with-code additionally preflights, deploys and smoke-checks its code bundle. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh image [nova\|buster\|both]` | Deploy selected agent images; omitted target means both. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh code [nova\|buster\|both]` | Deploy selected code bundles; omitted target means both. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh smoke` | Run Nova/Buster Pod-level smoke checks. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh smoke-agent <nova\|buster>` | Run Pod-level smoke checks for one named agent. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh status` | Show agents/infrastructure and enabled Prism status. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh prism-smoke` | Run Prism smoke checks. |
| `./scripts/deploy.sh prism-status` | Show Prism status. |

## Command Effects And Authority

The deployment commands above are not all read-only verification. Run them from
the repository root with the intended Kubernetes context and namespace selected.
The platform maintainer owns this deployment route; use the [CLI reference](cli.md)
and [operator procedure](../use/operate.md) for prerequisites and recovery.

| Command family | Effect and required authority | Expected observation and stop boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `image`, `image <name>` | Mutates the selected agent deployment through `cmd_image` → `deploy_agent` in image mode. Requires deployment write authority, not only permission to inspect pods. | Applies selected image/runtime values and waits for deployment health. A failure can follow partial mutation; inspect the selected release before recovery. Do not run as a read-only check. |
| `nova-production-preflights <image>` | Runs live production-suite preflights after source-cutover checks. Requires the individual preflights' cluster, execution and external-service authority; can create workloads, images and receipts. | Each required proof must succeed. Stop on failure; do not equate partial results with whole-suite acceptance or retry unknown external effects blindly. |
| `smoke`, `smoke-agent <name>` | Inspects deployed workloads, waits for readiness and executes gateway/health/file checks inside containers. Requires cluster read and pod-exec authority. `smoke` also checks Prism when enabled. | Successful checks establish only the tested pod/health boundary, not a full pipeline run. Diagnose a failed check before changing deployments. |
| `status` | Reads resource status; includes Prism status when enabled. Requires resource-read authority in the selected namespaces. | Displays observed resources, not functional pipeline acceptance. Missing or unhealthy resources require diagnosis, not an automatic redeploy. |

These effects follow the dispatch and `cmd_image`, `cmd_smoke_agent`, `cmd_smoke`,
`cmd_status` and `cmd_nova_production_preflights` implementations in
[scripts/deploy.sh](../../../scripts/deploy.sh). This documentation correction did not run commands against a live deployment.

## Local Documentation And Deployment Checks

```bash
npm run verify:plugin-system-v2
npm run typecheck:skills
npm run docs:inventory:check
npm run docs:generate:check
node tests/verification/deployment/check-deployment-truth.mjs --source-root "$PWD"
git diff --check
```

## Claim-To-Test Map

| Claim class | Source or verifier |
| --- | --- |
| Documentation inventory and generated references are current | `npm run docs:inventory:check`; `npm run docs:generate:check`; `node scripts/docs-check.mjs` |
| Core, package, capability, lifecycle, recovery, isolation, and malicious-package checks pass | `npm run verify:plugin-system-v2` |
| Deployment manifests, NetworkPolicies, service exposure, PVCs, config mounts, and sandbox surfaces match source | `node tests/verification/deployment/check-deployment-truth.mjs --source-root "$PWD"` |
| Documentation surface links and generated docs expectations stay valid | `npm run docs:check` |
| Restart, recovery, retry, crash, and resume behavior remain source-backed | `node tests/verification/contracts/check-plugin-system-v2-phase7.mjs`; `node tests/verification/contracts/check-plugin-system-v2-resume.mjs` |
| A selected real model-backed scenario and its cleanup satisfy their contracts | `npm run e2e:real:full`; read the exact command contract and its current STOP boundary below before execution |
| Proposed doc edits have no whitespace errors | `git diff --check` |
| Referenced source paths/config keys exist | Use a targeted `test -e`/ `rg -q` sanity check for newly cited paths and keys before closing the docs pass. |

## Read Before Running

These are command contracts, not successful execution records. Run repository commands from the repository root unless the entry specifies another place. A command name containing `check`, `test`, `live`, `production` or `--check` does not establish its effects or proof level. Read the exact entry before supplying credentials, choosing a cluster or running an aggregate. Arguments after `npm run <name> --` belong to its receiver; required arguments are not supplied by the alias. Child npm lifecycle hooks and inherited environment/configuration can affect execution. For an aggregate, all ordered children must finish, and each child retains its own scope and prerequisites.

After a failure or unknown external outcome, retain the run identity, original logs and partial state. The listed owner must reconcile those effects before retrying; exit zero can also mean an explicit skip, no-op or aborted confirmation. No reference entry grants a new live execution, promotion, deletion or human acceptance.

Use the [CLI reference](cli.md), [workflow inventory](workflows.md), [operator procedure](../use/operate.md) and [recovery procedure](../use/recovery.md) for the surrounding route.

### npm-60: npm run verify:test-gate:phase8

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check sandboxed direct commands, report adapters, suite resolution, local plan execution, and the controlled phase-eight unit path. |
| Scope | Compile native plugin sandbox launcher. Check actual command capability literal arguments, environment, file/network denial, limits and descendant cleanup. Exercise phase8-vertical controlled unit provider/report path through actual local Nova/Buster runtime. Check strict production Nova/Buster configuration, token/key/trust/dependency rejection and listener startup. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with locked dependencies and the executables required below. Child commands inherit caller environment, PATH, and Git configuration unless the receiver explicitly replaces them. Native cc with selected Linux headers/linker flags and writable destination. Git, /usr/bin/tar, native sandbox and installed runtime dependencies. Uses internally supplied PHASE7 token/key environment records; inherited process environment is not globally scrubbed. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Uses repository cwd; cc writes PID staging binary, failure removes staging and exits compiler status; success chmod755+rename replaces foundation/isolation/plugin-sandbox. Existing binary may remain after failed compile. Temporary real Node subprocesses and sandbox resource controls; attempts denied network/outside writes; finally shuts runner/removes temp. Temporary committed Git fixtures, generated keys, loopback HTTP runtime, native contained Node test/JUnit/LCOV commands and durable result/evidence. Inner finally stops runtime and outer finally removes tree. Temporary JSON and generated Ed25519 keys; starts/stops real loopback runtimes. Creates configuration-only registry/BuildKit readers; no build is launched. Finally removes tree. Ordered && chains stop at the first nonzero child; earlier files, processes, or remote effects are not rolled back as one transaction. |
| Expected result and limits | Compiler diagnostics on failure; successful file replacement without summary. JSON direct-command network denied and limits true. Structured phase summary after asserted expected decisions, including deliberately failed/advisory/skipped cases. JSON phase7-runtime-config. Not kernel/runtime isolation verification or host installation. Controlled local containment only, not arbitrary command or cgroup production grant. Controlled fixture only; not project test completeness, deployed cluster or production acceptance. Configuration/startup scope, not real build/push/deployed identity. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import) |
| When this changes | Change the command, its receiver/fixtures, and the affected subsystem contract together. Rerun the exact command with its declared native tools and authority; keep failure, skip, and cleanup outcomes. For generated outputs, use the owning native generation/check path rather than editing output files. |

### npm-63: npm run verify:test-gate:phase10

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check retirement/cutover assertions, controlled remote unit execution, scaffold migration, remote quality-gate packages, and the phase-nine chain. |
| Scope | Check absence of retired bridge/runtime and strict current configuration, plus Prism plan conversion. Compile native plugin sandbox launcher. Verify phase10-cutover selected replacement/source or contained execution responsibilities. Verify phase10-vertical selected replacement/source or contained execution responsibilities. Exercise actual project scaffold/apply and legacy migration/rejection with local fixtures. Validate complete unit baseline/ledger identities, dispositions, proof-path presence and source-only cutover. Check or generate exact selected parity Markdown report from its ledger. Check explicit direct-command suite resolution/configuration and forbidden environment/path/report conditions. Compare current real Node JUnit pass/fail/skip results to immutable recorded legacy comparison. Exercise phase9-vertical controlled unit provider/report path through actual local Nova/Buster runtime. Check actual command capability literal arguments, environment, file/network denial, limits and descendant cleanup. Exercise phase8-vertical controlled unit provider/report path through actual local Nova/Buster runtime. Check strict production Nova/Buster configuration, token/key/trust/dependency rejection and listener startup. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with locked dependencies and the executables required below. Child commands inherit caller environment, PATH, and Git configuration unless the receiver explicitly replaces them. Native cc with selected Linux headers/linker flags and writable destination. Node, /usr/bin/tar and actual scaffold implementation. Git, /usr/bin/tar, native sandbox and installed runtime dependencies. Uses internally supplied PHASE7 token/key environment records; inherited process environment is not globally scrubbed. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Reads repository sources/schema and imports Prism converter; no deployment invocation. Uses repository cwd; cc writes PID staging binary, failure removes staging and exits compiler status; success chmod755+rename replaces foundation/isolation/plugin-sandbox. Existing binary may remain after failed compile. Source inventory/ledger/status and current receiver/scaffold/deploy text assertions. No live production acceptance. No subprocess or network invocation in this receiver body. Creates temporary Git fixture and Ed25519 keys, starts real loopback Nova/Buster runtime, executes contained Node/JUnit commands and imports results. Stops runtime in inner finally; removes temporary tree in outer finally. Requires Git, /usr/bin/tar, native sandbox and actual runtime dependencies. No deployed cluster acceptance. Node children write generated progress.scaffold/progress/pipeline files only in temporary repos, tar controlled output, symlink negative; after hook removes roots, separate outside fixture finally removed. URLs are fixture plan data, not live requests. Read-only JSON/Markdown and file-presence assertions. Selected npm invocations include --check: read and compare exact Markdown, exit1 stale, no report write in those invocations. Default direct generator invocation writes target. Temporary provider fixture and injected capability response used only for negative/configuration assertions, then removed. Executes local passing/failing Node test fixtures, captures output and parses reports. Reads rather than reruns deleted legacy path. Temporary committed Git fixtures, generated keys, loopback HTTP runtime, native contained Node test/JUnit/LCOV commands and durable result/evidence. Inner finally stops runtime and outer finally removes tree. Temporary real Node subprocesses and sandbox resource controls; attempts denied network/outside writes; finally shuts runner/removes temp. Temporary JSON and generated Ed25519 keys; starts/stops real loopback runtimes. Creates configuration-only registry/BuildKit readers; no build is launched. Finally removes tree. Ordered && chains stop at the first nonzero child; earlier files, processes, or remote effects are not rolled back as one transaction. |
| Expected result and limits | JSON compatibility retired. Compiler diagnostics on failure; successful file replacement without summary. Receiver structured phase/cutover summary after exact assertions. Node TAP for selected tests after expected failures. JSON parityItems and disposition/status counts. Verified report diagnostic or stale exit1. JSON phase9 parity. JSON phase9 retained-comparison. Structured phase summary after asserted expected decisions, including deliberately failed/advisory/skipped cases. JSON direct-command network denied and limits true. JSON phase7-runtime-config. No current production acceptance. Not kernel/runtime isolation verification or host installation. No broad production acceptance; source-only, local and real external effects are distinguished in the effect description. Not actual deployment, project correctness or production migration. Proof paths are not executed; productionAcceptance remains pending-deployment. Record/report equality, not proof execution or current semantic acceptance. Not native command execution; legacy unit authority stays deleted. Expected failed child is part of successful comparison; zero is not all test cases passed. Controlled fixture only; not project test completeness, deployed cluster or production acceptance. Controlled local containment only, not arbitrary command or cgroup production grant. Configuration/startup scope, not real build/push/deployed identity. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import) |

### npm-64: npm run verify:test-gate:unit-live

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Run a real controlled unit process through Nova and remote Buster. |
| Scope | One known Node/JUnit testcase, durable remote execution, resource/report evidence, and result import; not a caller application test suite. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with Node and Git, KUBECLAW_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS selecting Buster test.plan.execute via buster-plan-v1, BUSTER_V2_TOKEN, and BUSTER_SOURCE_ATTESTATION_PRIVATE_KEY. The endpoint must be the approved exact HTTP(S) origin; URL userinfo/path/query/fragment are not a substitute for the authority contract.  |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | The remote unit process writes the known JUnit report and gate/evidence state. The helper uses a temporary committed local fixture/state and removes its owned local directory in finally. Real remote writes can precede a failure; local deletion does not reverse them. No command is executed by this reference. |
| Expected result and limits | Unsigned nova-unit-production-preflight.v2 JSON is printed only after the completed/passed remote decision, imported evidence, and required provider assertions. This helper does not select a Kubernetes fixture or browser and does not sign a final receipt. Direct npm does not run deploy.sh receipt signing or its additional independent cluster cleanup. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import) |
| When this changes | Change this helper, its fixture, provider configuration, remote receiver, resource/cleanup contract, or evidence fields together; rerun this exact direct helper with the intended authority and inspect the original job/resource outcome before retrying an uncertain request. |

### npm-67: npm run verify:test-gate:manifest-lint-parity-ledger

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check manifest-lint parity ledger completeness and replacement dispositions. |
| Scope | Validate exact selected baseline/ledger identifiers, dispositions, proof-path presence, source authority and explicit accepted deferrals. Check or generate exact selected parity Markdown report from its ledger. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with locked dependencies and the executables required below. Child commands inherit caller environment, PATH, and Git configuration unless the receiver explicitly replaces them.  |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Read-only parse/assert; referenced proofs are checked for existence, not executed. Selected npm invocations include --check: read and compare exact Markdown, exit1 stale, no report write in those invocations. Default direct generator invocation writes target. Ordered && chains stop at the first nonzero child; earlier files, processes, or remote effects are not rolled back as one transaction. |
| Expected result and limits | JSON suite/item/disposition/authority summary. Verified report diagnostic or stale exit1. No fresh live acceptance; planned deferral remains open. Record/report equality, not proof execution or current semantic acceptance. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import) |
| When this changes | Change the command, its receiver/fixtures, and the affected subsystem contract together. Rerun the exact command with its declared native tools and authority; keep failure, skip, and cleanup outcomes. For generated outputs, use the owning native generation/check path rather than editing output files. |

Finally removes tree (initial setup before try may remain on failure). Reads repository sources/schema and imports Prism converter; no deployment invocation. ### npm-71: npm run verify:test-gate:container-build-implementation

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check registered container-build plan construction and implementation contracts without invoking BuildKit. |
| Scope | Validate the recorded container-build baseline schema, identity/count and selected state constraints. Compile native plugin sandbox launcher. Validate native container-build constructor policy and implementation markers. Verify container-build-implementation selected replacement/source or contained execution responsibilities. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with locked dependencies and the executables required below. Child commands inherit caller environment, PATH, and Git configuration unless the receiver explicitly replaces them. Native cc with selected Linux headers/linker flags and writable destination. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Reads bounded baseline and, where selected, policy/guide-presence records; no proof execution. Uses repository cwd; cc writes PID staging binary, failure removes staging and exits compiler status; success chmod755+rename replaces foundation/isolation/plugin-sandbox. Existing binary may remain after failed compile. Temporary root, constructors and source assertions; finally deletes root. Discovers local trusted plugin registrations and resolves typed container-build plan; source-pattern assertions inspect implementation. Does not invoke BuildKit or push an image. Ordered && chains stop at the first nonzero child; earlier files, processes, or remote effects are not rolled back as one transaction. The selected provider-registry child creates an OS temporary `test-provider-registry-*` workspace and does not remove the workspace: successful execution retains the `unit` and invalid `bad-schema` package fixtures; failures may retain the earlier partial tree. Selected negative cases remove their own subdirectories only. Cleanup of other implementation/parity fixtures does not remove this separate workspace. Preserve diagnostics and identify the exact inactive owned path before cleanup. |
| Expected result and limits | Structured baseline identity/count summary. Compiler diagnostics on failure; successful file replacement without summary. JSON runtime container-build real-buildctl-only describes supported route. Receiver structured phase/cutover summary after exact assertions. Record consistency is not current live parity or application quality. Not kernel/runtime isolation verification or host installation. Does not launch buildctl or perform registry verification itself. No broad production acceptance; source-only, local and real external effects are distinguished in the effect description. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import) |
| When this changes | Change the command, its receiver/fixtures, and the affected subsystem contract together. Rerun the exact command with its declared native tools and authority; keep failure, skip, and cleanup outcomes. For generated outputs, use the owning native generation/check path rather than editing output files. |

No actual cluster rollout; source-pattern assertions do not execute controller. ### npm-87: npm run verify:test-gate:kubernetes-fixture-live

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Verify a retained Kubernetes workload and approved Secret through Nova/Buster. |
| Scope | Manifest copy, digest-pinned workload deployment, readiness, Secret projection, imported outputs, and retained lease identity. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with Node and Git, KUBECLAW_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS selecting Buster test.plan.execute via buster-plan-v1, BUSTER_V2_TOKEN, and BUSTER_SOURCE_ATTESTATION_PRIVATE_KEY. The endpoint must be the approved exact HTTP(S) origin; URL userinfo/path/query/fragment are not a substitute for the authority contract. KUBECLAW_KUBERNETES_PREFLIGHT_IMAGE and KUBECLAW_KUBERNETES_PREFLIGHT_SECRET must name the approved digest image and existing Secret. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Create a temporary committed manifest and send a signed plan that creates real leased workload resources and copies the approved Secret. Retention is retain/600 seconds. The helper uses a temporary committed local fixture/state and removes its owned local directory in finally. Real remote writes can precede a failure; local deletion does not reverse them. No command is executed by this reference. |
| Expected result and limits | Unsigned kubernetes-fixture-production-preflight.v1 JSON is printed only after the completed/passed remote decision, imported evidence, and required provider assertions. The helper leaves explicit cleanupVerified=false and clusterCleanupObserved=false. It does not delete the retained lease or prove namespace absence; deploy.sh adds those operations. Readiness is not business functionality. Direct npm does not run deploy.sh receipt signing or its additional independent cluster cleanup. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import) |
| When this changes | Change this helper, its fixture, provider configuration, remote receiver, resource/cleanup contract, or evidence fields together; rerun this exact direct helper with the intended authority and inspect the original job/resource outcome before retrying an uncertain request. |

```text
node tests/verification/e2e/nova-kubernetes-fixture-production-preflight.mts
```

### npm-89: npm run verify:test-gate:http-implementation

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Validate the recorded http baseline schema, identity/count and selected state constraints.; Compile native plugin sandbox launcher.; Exercise actual http provider/plan validation and local service observation.; Check provider discovery/registry/configuration invariants; Check project/schema/operator-field textual coverage; Check discovered declared error identifiers occur in reference/user guides; Validate selected example provider configurations with actual Ajv2020 schemas; Check selected migration prose for bounded language rules |
| Scope | Validate the recorded http baseline schema, identity/count and selected state constraints. Compile native plugin sandbox launcher. Exercise actual http provider/plan validation and local service observation. These selected documentation children (verify:docs:controlled-language, verify:docs:error-codes, verify:docs:examples, verify:docs:schema-fields) enumerate every immediate *-documentation-manifest.json under docs/architecture and audit its declared cross-suite documents/sources, not only this provider. docs-language also reads the migration playbook and templates. Schema/error presence, AJV example validation and controlled-language checks retain their distinct scopes; they do not execute the demonstrated examples. The selected HTTP package executes its actual http-provider-live.test.ts loopback provider/capability/resolver assertions. The inherited tail also runs the provider-registry check and npx tsc --noEmit -p skills/common/plugin-runtime/tsconfig.json, in addition to the named documentation audits. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with locked dependencies and the executables required below. Child commands inherit caller environment, PATH, and Git configuration unless the receiver explicitly replaces them. Native cc with selected Linux headers/linker flags and writable destination. The selected HTTP package and implementation use native loopback HTTP, not a browser or Lighthouse; no Lighthouse executable path is required by this command. All selected documentation manifests and their declared documents, schema/error/example sources, playbook/templates and installed AJV2020/format dependencies must be readable. Missing inputs or failed assertions are real failures, not skipped checks. The actual package test needs a free loopback port, compatible native TypeScript Node exports, installed Nova/Buster contract dependencies and its current builtin provider manifests. The runtime typecheck uses the installed locked TypeScript compiler; no browser or Lighthouse path is required. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | The selected baseline/source-marker checks do not execute referenced proofs. Their documentation children have the separate cross-manifest read scope described above. Uses repository cwd; cc writes PID staging binary, failure removes staging and exits compiler status; success chmod755+rename replaces foundation/isolation/plugin-sandbox. Existing binary may remain after failed compile. Temporary local files, real loopback HTTP service and provider execution; actual HTTP requests; server/tree cleanup in final path, but setup before guard can fail leaving resources. Ordered && chains stop at the first nonzero child; earlier files, processes, or remote effects are not rolled back as one transaction. The selected verify:docs:* children read manifest-declared repository documents/schemas/source and validate their own text/example inputs; they do not run the commands demonstrated by those documents. The HTTP package starts an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 server, invokes the real HTTP provider/capability against controlled endpoints, reads builtin manifests for real resolution and closes the server in finally. It exercises timeout, redirect/size, origin/method/header and typed-fixture boundaries. The provider-registry child validates declared registrations and the TypeScript noEmit child checks the plugin runtime without emitting application code. The selected provider-registry child creates an OS temporary `test-provider-registry-*` workspace and does not remove the workspace: successful execution retains the `unit` and invalid `bad-schema` package fixtures; failures may retain the earlier partial tree. Selected negative cases remove their own subdirectories only. Cleanup of other implementation/parity fixtures does not remove this separate workspace. Preserve diagnostics and identify the exact inactive owned path before cleanup. Of these four documentation children, only docs-examples compiles AJV validators; the schema/error/language modes perform their declared local structural/text checks. |
| Expected result and limits | Structured baseline identity/count summary. Compiler diagnostics on failure; successful file replacement without summary. Structured implementation summary after controlled assertions. Record consistency is not current live parity or application quality. Not kernel/runtime isolation verification or host installation. Only controlled local target; not deployed app acceptance or universal provider correctness. Each selected docs mode must print `suite migration docs-<mode> check passed` and exit zero; failures list their native diagnostics and exit nonzero. This is only its declared source/text/schema-example audit, not runtime or whole-language acceptance. The package finishes only after its native assertions and prints JSON ok:true/provider:http/boundary:real-local-http-server/mocks:0/wrappers:0. The registry assertions and TypeScript compiler must also exit zero; an HTTP success cannot replace those child results. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import); [documentation](../extend/documentation-maintenance.md) |
| When this changes | Change the command, its receiver/fixtures, and the affected subsystem contract together. Rerun the exact command with its declared native tools and authority; keep failure, skip, and cleanup outcomes. For generated outputs, use the owning native generation/check path rather than editing output files. Changes to any selected cross-suite documentation manifest or declared input require its corresponding verify:docs:* child and requalification of this composed route, not just the HTTP/provider-specific receiver. |

Underlying command definition. This is source data, not an instruction to run it.

```text
npm run verify:test-gate:http-baseline && npm run plugin-system:sandbox:build && npm test --prefix skills/buster/plugins/http && node tests/verification/contracts/check-pipeline-http-implementation.mts && npm run verify:test-gate:provider-registry && npx tsc --noEmit -p skills/common/plugin-runtime/tsconfig.json && npm run verify:docs:schema-fields && npm run verify:docs:error-codes && npm run verify:docs:examples && npm run verify:docs:controlled-language
```

It does not establish arbitrary API or browser behavior. Direct npm does not run deploy.sh receipt signing or its additional independent cluster cleanup. |

### npm-96: npm run verify:test-gate:api-parity

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check API provider implementation and recorded parity decisions against controlled API receiver results. |
| Scope | Validate the recorded api baseline schema, identity/count and selected state constraints. Compile native plugin sandbox launcher. Exercise actual api provider/plan validation and local service observation. Validate exact selected baseline/ledger identifiers, dispositions, proof-path presence, source authority and explicit accepted deferrals. Validate api parity inventory and current proof/scenario references. These selected documentation children (verify:docs:controlled-language, verify:docs:error-codes, verify:docs:examples, verify:docs:schema-fields) enumerate every immediate *-documentation-manifest.json under docs/architecture and audit its declared cross-suite documents/sources, not only this provider. docs-language also reads the migration playbook and templates. Schema/error presence, AJV example validation and controlled-language checks retain their distinct scopes; they do not execute the demonstrated examples. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with locked dependencies and the executables required below. Child commands inherit caller environment, PATH, and Git configuration unless the receiver explicitly replaces them. Native cc with selected Linux headers/linker flags and writable destination. Browser engines and installed native modules required where used; Lighthouse fixed /ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1228 path must exist. All selected documentation manifests and their declared documents, schema/error/example sources, playbook/templates and installed AJV2020/format dependencies must be readable. Missing inputs or failed assertions are real failures, not skipped checks. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | The selected baseline/source-marker checks do not execute referenced proofs. Their documentation children have the separate cross-manifest read scope described above. Uses repository cwd; cc writes PID staging binary, failure removes staging and exits compiler status; success chmod755+rename replaces foundation/isolation/plugin-sandbox. Existing binary may remain after failed compile. Temporary local files, real loopback HTTP service and provider execution; actual HTTP requests; server/tree cleanup in final path, but setup before guard can fail leaving resources. Read-only parse/assert; referenced proofs are checked for existence, not executed. Reads baseline/ledger, proof presence and selected source markers; no referenced proof invocation in this receiver. Ordered && chains stop at the first nonzero child; earlier files, processes, or remote effects are not rolled back as one transaction. The selected verify:docs:* children read manifest-declared repository documents/schemas/source and validate their own text/example inputs; they do not run the commands demonstrated by those documents. The selected provider-registry child creates an OS temporary `test-provider-registry-*` workspace and does not remove the workspace: successful execution retains the `unit` and invalid `bad-schema` package fixtures; failures may retain the earlier partial tree. Selected negative cases remove their own subdirectories only. Cleanup of other implementation/parity fixtures does not remove this separate workspace. Preserve diagnostics and identify the exact inactive owned path before cleanup. Of these four documentation children, only docs-examples compiles AJV validators; the schema/error/language modes perform their declared local structural/text checks. |
| Expected result and limits | Structured baseline identity/count summary. Compiler diagnostics on failure; successful file replacement without summary. Structured implementation summary after controlled assertions. JSON suite/item/disposition/authority summary. Structured parity item summary. Record consistency is not current live parity or application quality. Not kernel/runtime isolation verification or host installation. Only controlled local target; not deployed app acceptance or universal provider correctness. No fresh live acceptance; planned deferral remains open. Proof-path/source-marker presence alone is not execution or fresh production acceptance. Each selected docs mode must print `suite migration docs-<mode> check passed` and exit zero; failures list their native diagnostics and exit nonzero. This is only its declared source/text/schema-example audit, not runtime or whole-language acceptance. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import); [documentation](../extend/documentation-maintenance.md) |
| When this changes | Change the command, its receiver/fixtures, and the affected subsystem contract together. Rerun the exact command with its declared native tools and authority; keep failure, skip, and cleanup outcomes. For generated outputs, use the owning native generation/check path rather than editing output files. Changes to any selected cross-suite documentation manifest or declared input require its corresponding verify:docs:* child and requalification of this composed route, not just the HTTP/provider-specific receiver. |

### npm-100: npm run verify:test-gate:a11y-parity

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Validate the recorded a11y baseline schema, identity/count and selected state constraints.; Compile native plugin sandbox launcher.; Exercise actual a11y provider/plan validation and local service observation.; Validate exact selected baseline/ledger identifiers, dispositions, proof-path presence, source authority and explicit accepted deferrals.; Validate a11y parity inventory and current proof/scenario references.; Check provider discovery/registry/configuration invariants; Check project/schema/operator-field textual coverage; Check discovered declared error identifiers occur in reference/user guides; Validate selected example provider configurations with actual Ajv2020 schemas; Check selected migration prose for bounded language rules |
| Scope | Validate the recorded a11y baseline schema, identity/count and selected state constraints. Compile native plugin sandbox launcher. Exercise actual a11y provider/plan validation and local service observation. Validate exact selected baseline/ledger identifiers, dispositions, proof-path presence, source authority and explicit accepted deferrals. Validate a11y parity inventory and current proof/scenario references. These selected documentation children (verify:docs:controlled-language, verify:docs:error-codes, verify:docs:examples, verify:docs:schema-fields) enumerate every immediate *-documentation-manifest.json under docs/architecture and audit its declared cross-suite documents/sources, not only this provider. docs-language also reads the migration playbook and templates. Schema/error presence, AJV example validation and controlled-language checks retain their distinct scopes; they do not execute the demonstrated examples. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with locked dependencies and the executables required below. Child commands inherit caller environment, PATH, and Git configuration unless the receiver explicitly replaces them. Native cc with selected Linux headers/linker flags and writable destination. Browser engines and installed native modules required where used; Lighthouse fixed /ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1228 path must exist. All selected documentation manifests and their declared documents, schema/error/example sources, playbook/templates and installed AJV2020/format dependencies must be readable. Missing inputs or failed assertions are real failures, not skipped checks. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | The selected baseline/source-marker checks do not execute referenced proofs. Their documentation children have the separate cross-manifest read scope described above. Uses repository cwd; cc writes PID staging binary, failure removes staging and exits compiler status; success chmod755+rename replaces foundation/isolation/plugin-sandbox. Existing binary may remain after failed compile. Temporary local files, real loopback HTTP service and provider execution; real Chromium/Axe browser; server/tree cleanup in final path, but setup before guard can fail leaving resources. Read-only parse/assert; referenced proofs are checked for existence, not executed. Reads baseline/ledger, proof presence and selected source markers; no referenced proof invocation in this receiver. Ordered && chains stop at the first nonzero child; earlier files, processes, or remote effects are not rolled back as one transaction. The selected verify:docs:* children read manifest-declared repository documents/schemas/source and validate their own text/example inputs; they do not run the commands demonstrated by those documents. The selected provider-registry child creates an OS temporary `test-provider-registry-*` workspace and does not remove the workspace: successful execution retains the `unit` and invalid `bad-schema` package fixtures; failures may retain the earlier partial tree. Selected negative cases remove their own subdirectories only. Cleanup of other implementation/parity fixtures does not remove this separate workspace. Preserve diagnostics and identify the exact inactive owned path before cleanup. Of these four documentation children, only docs-examples compiles AJV validators; the schema/error/language modes perform their declared local structural/text checks. |
| Expected result and limits | Structured baseline identity/count summary. Compiler diagnostics on failure; successful file replacement without summary. Structured implementation summary after controlled assertions. JSON suite/item/disposition/authority summary. Structured parity item summary. Record consistency is not current live parity or application quality. Not kernel/runtime isolation verification or host installation. Only controlled local target; not deployed app acceptance or universal provider correctness. No fresh live acceptance; planned deferral remains open. Proof-path/source-marker presence alone is not execution or fresh production acceptance. Each selected docs mode must print `suite migration docs-<mode> check passed` and exit zero; failures list their native diagnostics and exit nonzero. This is only its declared source/text/schema-example audit, not runtime or whole-language acceptance. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import); [documentation](../extend/documentation-maintenance.md) |
| When this changes | Change the command, its receiver/fixtures, and the affected subsystem contract together. Rerun the exact command with its declared native tools and authority; keep failure, skip, and cleanup outcomes. For generated outputs, use the owning native generation/check path rather than editing output files. Changes to any selected cross-suite documentation manifest or declared input require its corresponding verify:docs:* child and requalification of this composed route, not just the HTTP/provider-specific receiver. |

```text
npm run verify:test-gate:a11y-implementation && node scripts/check-suite-parity-ledger.mjs docs/architecture/pipeline-test-gate-a11y-baseline.json docs/architecture/pipeline-test-gate-a11y-parity-ledger.json && node tests/verification/contracts/check-pipeline-a11y-parity.mts
```

### npm-102: npm run verify:test-gate:a11y-live

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Verify Axe accessibility checks in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit through Nova/Buster. |
| Scope | A checked manifest and leased digest-pinned HTTP fixture feed three real browser engine checks with imported evidence. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with Node and Git, KUBECLAW_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS selecting Buster test.plan.execute via buster-plan-v1, BUSTER_V2_TOKEN, and BUSTER_SOURCE_ATTESTATION_PRIVATE_KEY. The endpoint must be the approved exact HTTP(S) origin; URL userinfo/path/query/fragment are not a substitute for the authority contract. KUBECLAW_A11Y_PREFLIGHT_IMAGE must name the approved digest-pinned workload image; remote browser runtimes must be available. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Write committed fixture/browser profiles and gate state, deploy a leased workload, and launch actual browser/Axe processes. The helper uses a temporary committed local fixture/state and removes its owned local directory in finally. Real remote writes can precede a failure; local deletion does not reverse them. No command is executed by this reference. |
| Expected result and limits | Unsigned nova-a11y-production-preflight.v1 JSON is printed only after the completed/passed remote decision, imported evidence, and required provider assertions. Require all three engine identities. cleanupVerified=false and clusterCleanupObserved=false remain explicit; fixture accessibility is not whole-product or human usability. Direct npm does not run deploy.sh receipt signing or its additional independent cluster cleanup. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import) |
| When this changes | Change this helper, its fixture, provider configuration, remote receiver, resource/cleanup contract, or evidence fields together; rerun this exact direct helper with the intended authority and inspect the original job/resource outcome before retrying an uncertain request. |

### npm-107: npm run verify:test-gate:lighthouse-live

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Verify Lighthouse measurements of a leased fixture through Nova/Buster. |
| Scope | Checked manifest, leased digest-pinned HTTP workload, selected Lighthouse settings, and three imported reports. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with Node and Git, KUBECLAW_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS selecting Buster test.plan.execute via buster-plan-v1, BUSTER_V2_TOKEN, and BUSTER_SOURCE_ATTESTATION_PRIVATE_KEY. The endpoint must be the approved exact HTTP(S) origin; URL userinfo/path/query/fragment are not a substitute for the authority contract. KUBECLAW_LIGHTHOUSE_PREFLIGHT_IMAGE must name the approved digest-pinned workload image; the remote Lighthouse runtime is required. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Write committed fixture/settings and local gate state, deploy a leased workload, and execute actual Lighthouse measurements. The helper uses a temporary committed local fixture/state and removes its owned local directory in finally. Real remote writes can precede a failure; local deletion does not reverse them. No command is executed by this reference. |
| Expected result and limits | Unsigned nova-lighthouse-production-preflight.v1 JSON is printed only after the completed/passed remote decision, imported evidence, and required provider assertions. Assertions bind Lighthouse 13.4.1 and three reports. cleanupVerified=false and clusterCleanupObserved=false remain explicit; fixture results are not a continuing production performance guarantee. Direct npm does not run deploy.sh receipt signing or its additional independent cluster cleanup. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import) |
| When this changes | Change this helper, its fixture, provider configuration, remote receiver, resource/cleanup contract, or evidence fields together; rerun this exact direct helper with the intended authority and inspect the original job/resource outcome before retrying an uncertain request. |

### npm-112: npm run verify:test-gate:visual-live

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Verify visual comparison against the committed fixture baseline through Nova/Buster. |
| Scope | Strict visual comparison for home-desktop using the actual baseline/profile identities and imported browser evidence. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with Node and Git, KUBECLAW_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS selecting Buster test.plan.execute via buster-plan-v1, BUSTER_V2_TOKEN, and BUSTER_SOURCE_ATTESTATION_PRIVATE_KEY. The endpoint must be the approved exact HTTP(S) origin; URL userinfo/path/query/fragment are not a substitute for the authority contract. KUBECLAW_VISUAL_PREFLIGHT_IMAGE must name the approved digest-pinned image; committed baseline and actual browser versions must pass their checks. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Copy/commit the visual fixture, write gate state, deploy a leased workload, and capture/compare real browser output. The helper uses a temporary committed local fixture/state and removes its owned local directory in finally. Real remote writes can precede a failure; local deletion does not reverse them. No command is executed by this reference. |
| Expected result and limits | Unsigned nova-visual-production-preflight.v1 JSON is printed only after the completed/passed remote decision, imported evidence, and required provider assertions. A nonempty browser version and baseline compatibility are required. cleanupVerified=false and clusterCleanupObserved=false remain explicit; this does not accept the whole UI. Direct npm does not run deploy.sh receipt signing or its additional independent cluster cleanup. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import) |
| When this changes | Change this helper, its fixture, provider configuration, remote receiver, resource/cleanup contract, or evidence fields together; rerun this exact direct helper with the intended authority and inspect the original job/resource outcome before retrying an uncertain request. |

| Scope | Validate the recorded e2e baseline schema, identity/count and selected state constraints. Compile native plugin sandbox launcher. Validate e2e provider registration, suite resolution and actual runtime/source contract markers. Exercise e2e actual provider through local authenticated Nova/Buster remote boundary. These selected documentation children (verify:docs:controlled-language, verify:docs:error-codes, verify:docs:examples, verify:docs:schema-fields) enumerate every immediate *-documentation-manifest.json under docs/architecture and audit its declared cross-suite documents/sources, not only this provider. docs-language also reads the migration playbook and templates. Schema/error presence, AJV example validation and controlled-language checks retain their distinct scopes; they do not execute the demonstrated examples. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with locked dependencies and the executables required below. Child commands inherit caller environment, PATH, and Git configuration unless the receiver explicitly replaces them. Native cc with selected Linux headers/linker flags and writable destination. Security requires real cache (KUBECLAW_SECURITY_TEST_CACHE or known cache paths) and KUBECLAW_SECURITY_TEST_TRIVY/default executable; browsers require installed engines/CLI. All selected documentation manifests and their declared documents, schema/error/example sources, playbook/templates and installed AJV2020/format dependencies must be readable. Missing inputs or failed assertions are real failures, not skipped checks. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | The selected baseline/source-marker checks do not execute referenced proofs. Their documentation children have the separate cross-manifest read scope described above. Uses repository cwd; cc writes PID staging binary, failure removes staging and exits compiler status; success chmod755+rename replaces foundation/isolation/plugin-sandbox. Existing binary may remain after failed compile. Reads local sources/examples and resolves registered plan; does not capture browser in this implementation body. Temporary committed Git fixture, keys/durable stores and loopback runtime; real browser capture/report; stops runtime and deletes fixture in finally. Ordered && chains stop at the first nonzero child; earlier files, processes, or remote effects are not rolled back as one transaction. The selected verify:docs:* children read manifest-declared repository documents/schemas/source and validate their own text/example inputs; they do not run the commands demonstrated by those documents. The selected provider-registry child creates an OS temporary `test-provider-registry-*` workspace and does not remove the workspace: successful execution retains the `unit` and invalid `bad-schema` package fixtures; failures may retain the earlier partial tree. Selected negative cases remove their own subdirectories only. Cleanup of other implementation/parity fixtures does not remove this separate workspace. Preserve diagnostics and identify the exact inactive owned path before cleanup. Of these four documentation children, only docs-examples compiles AJV validators; the schema/error/language modes perform their declared local structural/text checks. |
| Expected result and limits | Structured baseline identity/count summary. Compiler diagnostics on failure; successful file replacement without summary. Structured implementation summary. Structured authenticatedDispatch/evidenceImported summary after result assertions. Record consistency is not current live parity or application quality. Not kernel/runtime isolation verification or host installation. Browser execution lives in selected package/remote-vertical delegates, not this source-marker proof. Local contained fixture, not deployed cluster, current release or all application checks. Each selected docs mode must print `suite migration docs-<mode> check passed` and exit zero; failures list their native diagnostics and exit nonzero. This is only its declared source/text/schema-example audit, not runtime or whole-language acceptance. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import); [documentation](../extend/documentation-maintenance.md) |
| When this changes | Change the command, its receiver/fixtures, and the affected subsystem contract together. Rerun the exact command with its declared native tools and authority; keep failure, skip, and cleanup outcomes. For generated outputs, use the owning native generation/check path rather than editing output files. Changes to any selected cross-suite documentation manifest or declared input require its corresponding verify:docs:* child and requalification of this composed route, not just the HTTP/provider-specific receiver. |

### npm-117: npm run verify:test-gate:e2e-live

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Verify a controlled Playwright journey through Nova/Buster. |
| Scope | Chromium checks the leased nginx fixture body; its Service port is 18080 and resource enforcement must be cgroup-v2. This is not the full model-backed pipeline journey. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository with Node and Git, KUBECLAW_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS selecting Buster test.plan.execute via buster-plan-v1, BUSTER_V2_TOKEN, and BUSTER_SOURCE_ATTESTATION_PRIVATE_KEY. The endpoint must be the approved exact HTTP(S) origin; URL userinfo/path/query/fragment are not a substitute for the authority contract. KUBECLAW_E2E_PREFLIGHT_IMAGE must name the approved digest-pinned image; remote Playwright/Chromium and cgroup-v2 support are required. PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_BASE_URL is supplied to the fixture browser configuration. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Commit the checked manifest/browser test and local gate state, deploy a real leased workload, and run Playwright. The helper uses a temporary committed local fixture/state and removes its owned local directory in finally. Real remote writes can precede a failure; local deletion does not reverse them. No command is executed by this reference. |
| Expected result and limits | Unsigned nova-e2e-production-preflight.v1 JSON is printed only after the completed/passed remote decision, imported evidence, and required provider assertions. The direct helper can emit unsigned JSON with servicePort=18080; it does not invoke the signer that separately rejects that port in the deploy wrapper. cleanupVerified=false and clusterCleanupObserved=false remain explicit. Never relabel an old signed receipt as this run. Direct npm does not run deploy.sh receipt signing or its additional independent cluster cleanup. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import) |
| When this changes | Change this helper, its fixture, provider configuration, remote receiver, resource/cleanup contract, or evidence fields together; rerun this exact direct helper with the intended authority and inspect the original job/resource outcome before retrying an uncertain request. |

No command is executed by this reference. |

All five outcomes and no blocking runtime findings are required. cleanupVerified=false and clusterCleanupObserved=false remain explicit. A point-in-time fixture scan is not perpetual or all-source security assurance. Direct npm does not run deploy.sh receipt signing or its additional independent cluster cleanup. |

The normal baseline requires current generated inventory matching its own selected committed sourceRevision; copied mutation fixtures deliberately use both isolation environment controls. No root pre/post hooks declared. Children inherit caller environment; missing native tools, source custody or baseline equality stops the route. The selected static PostgreSQL renderer also requires tar and a private writable OS temporary chart cache. A matching cached archive is reverified; a cache miss requires curl and HTTPS access to the locked chart transport (the selected PostgreSQL lock uses immutable Docker Hub OCI manifest/layer acquisition; supported HTTPS archive locks use direct HTTPS). Node parses Go source statically; these direct platform commands do not invoke a Go binary. Other aggregate/CI delegates retain their separately declared Go/tool prerequisites. Native source custody and normal publication require distinct preparation states. The supported maintenance sequence is clean committed Source and native platform generation/check first, then npm run sync-contract --prefix skills/common/plugins/openclaw-agent-observer to prepare publication runtime imports from the same committed contracts/agent-observability/v1/src. This original sync removes/recreates only its ignored src/generated/agent-observability target and copies canonical files; verify exact canonical file set/bytes. It is not an automatic hook of this platform command. Before any later clean native check, remove only an unchanged verified-owned generated copy after its consumers have stopped; never remove canonical Source or unrelated data. Separate staged successes do not establish simultaneous filesystem compatibility or successful execution of a containing docs:check/docs:publish-check/CI pipeline. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Runs the registered Node test files: source extraction reads actual declarations without runtime owner execution; custody cases create and commit private temporary Git fixtures, mutate product/registry bytes and aliases, then remove their own roots in finally. The outer runner enumerates tracked+untracked nonignored workspace files, copies sources preserving symlinks into its OS temporary parent and links installed node_modules. It repeatedly runs native inventory/Helm/Git reads in that owned fixture; policy cases inspect actual projected values or required projection refusals, check exact drift diagnostics, restore original bytes and recheck restored green policy fixtures. Original surface cases, combined Ingress and map-review negatives remain. Temporary parent is removed in finally and SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers; cleanup can fail, and an unexpected abrupt termination is not proof of removal. No shared source mutation, cluster operation, backup, migration, store retirement or live endpoint behavior is authorized by these synthetic mutations. The selected local child-renderer closure includes LiteLLM configuration rendering and PostgreSQL recovery-manifest rendering; its imported volume preflight is not called because this producer does not pass --preflight. PostgreSQL service selection stages a versions.json-pinned chart in os.tmpdir()/kubeclaw-infrastructure-charts-<uid>, requiring a real owner-private directory. Existing archives are size/SHA/name/version/appVersion checked with tar; absent archives trigger curl HTTPS/OCI acquisition, bounded manifest/layer/digest checks and archive verification before rename into the retained cache. Helm performs an offline template/upgrade-view render with the local image post-renderer; the render-only password marker must not escape into resources, and reserved images must match pinned versions. It does not run PostgreSQL, backup SQL/shell or kubectl. Owned download-* directories are removed in finally; the private cache and verified archive remain, including after a later producer/check/mutation failure. Bad existing cache/archive, missing tools, network/acquisition, digest, archive identity, image or rendering failures stop; no automatic bad-cache repair or whole-cache rollback is promised. Thus --check compares normal outputs without writing them but is not filesystem-readonly or necessarily network-free. Repeated mutation calls can reuse/populate this separate cache; removing the owned mutation/Git fixture does not remove it. The rendered-policy helper receives these already acquired resources without starting tools or runtime owners. It selects one exact source/origin/kind/name/namespace, requires own-field paths and declared nested identities, and parses embedded registry ConfigMap YAML only as one valid unique-key/no-alias document. Missing/ambiguous resources or fields and identity changes stop. Values retain selected native resource provenance, conditional/fixture limits and outer Source authentication; declaration location is not misrepresented as selected-field offset. Original templates are not executed as arbitrary JavaScript or reimplemented by a scanner. Repeated native inventory calls also perform the separate conditional Helm comparison; its sizing inputs are render fixtures, not selected defaults. Registered rendered-policy helper tests read real registry manifests and synthetic resource copies without cluster deployment or runtime cleanup. |
| Expected result and limits | The registered source/custody tests and baseline must succeed; every source-defined operation must run, produce exactly its expected diagnostic and satisfy applicable value/projection-refusal/restoration assertions. Final JSON ok:true reports baseline:green, actual mutation results and mapReview negatives; wrong/missing diagnostics, unsupported literal grammar, changed selector identity, un-restored policy fixture or incomplete matrix fails. Limits: no real product rollout, complete internal algorithms, effective external retention or global source-purpose approval; this describes the receiver, not a claim this current full runner succeeded. |

Platform surface inventory maintainers and the named endpoint, event, store, Secret and Ops-tool subsystem owners must inspect complete diagnostics and partial effects, restore owned fixtures where applicable, and obtain independent review of the changed topic. Keep the declared environment, skips and STOP conditions; do not refresh expected data merely to hide a mismatch. Inspect exact Source-derived values versus fallbacks/effective unknowns, refusal diagnostics, owned-fixture restoration and a meaningful reader cleanup/STOP decision; obtain independent affected-topic review. Commit actual Source before explicit current-revision generation; preserve the shared lock and unrelated outputs. Do not refresh mappings/baselines to conceal mismatch. Changes to conditional render recipe, selected origin/resource/nested identity, embedded YAML grammar or public provenance labels require the focused rendered-policy source tests plus the real native Job-TTL, embedded-registry and conditional-quarantine value projection/refusal/restoration controls. A matching cached archive is reverified; a cache miss requires curl and HTTPS access to the locked chart transport (the selected PostgreSQL lock uses immutable Docker Hub OCI manifest/layer acquisition; supported HTTPS archive locks use direct HTTPS). ### npm-230: npm run verify:docs:controlled-language

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check selected migration prose for bounded language rules |
| Scope | Every immediate architecture documentation manifest; migration playbook/templates plus deduplicated selected user/operator/security prose/sections. |
| Environment and execution place | Repository root through npm, Node.js 24 as the canonical development handbook prescribes (not a package.json engines constraint) and installed module-resolvable ajv/dist/2020.js, ajv-formats and imported production-receipt-attestation dependencies (shared module imports even when this mode does not compile schemas). No AJV compilation, child process, demonstrated command or output writes. The shared attestation module statically imports only Node crypto/fs/url, declares its receipt helpers/constants, and guards its sign/verify CLI by its own import.meta.url matching process.argv[1]; that CLI branch is not selected when this migration checker imports it. No receipt signing, key read or CLI write is performed by the selected documentation mode. |

Limits: Not complete ASD-STE100 dictionary/writing-rule compliance or integrated editorial review. |

| When this changes | Changes to this mode’s manifest discovery, selected inputs or finite rule behavior select this exact command; check all affected immediate manifests, not just one provider. Preserve first diagnostics and correct the owning source before retry; no runtime or whole-language acceptance follows. |

### npm-232: npm run docs:check

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Run the repository documentation check aggregate. |
| Scope | Exact ordered child commands: docs:parity:transition:check, docs:status:check, docs:check:generated, docs:blueprint:check, docs:tree:check, docs:tree:mutations, docs:check:refs, docs:site-boundary:check, docs:check:coverage, docs:publication:check, verify:migration:workflow. Direct Node stages, if present, remain part of the exact command shown. Delegated platform-inventory checking also derives typed store-policy declarations and source/caller joins; its alias is not store-only. Platform policy acquisition also uses the existing selected native Helm/static resources and one separate policy-only Prism ingestion comparison, labelled helm:prism-ingestion-policy: ingestion.enabled is enabled with a typed boolean override, explicit render-only CPU/memory sizing and the existing native-worker fixture settings. The maintained selected Prism profile still disables ingestion. This comparison supplies only policy selection and is never merged into the original selected resource/signal/endpoint arrays; it is not a deployment, inferred default or observed capacity. |
| Environment and execution place | Run at the repository root with the combined prerequisites of the listed child commands. npm inherits the caller environment. The shell executes && stages in order and stops at the first nonzero result. The platform child selects its existing inventory sourceRevision before the shared-lock fallback, verifies cited producer/authority bytes, and does not silently select HEAD or update the shared lock. Optional explicit current-HEAD source-first generation is a separate producer invocation, not an automatic aggregate action. The selected static PostgreSQL renderer also requires tar and a private writable OS temporary chart cache. A matching cached archive is reverified; a cache miss requires curl and HTTPS access to the locked chart transport (the selected PostgreSQL lock uses immutable Docker Hub OCI manifest/layer acquisition; supported HTTPS archive locks use direct HTTPS). Node parses Go source statically; these direct platform commands do not invoke a Go binary. Other aggregate/CI delegates retain their separately declared Go/tool prerequisites. Native source custody and normal publication require distinct preparation states. The supported maintenance sequence is clean committed Source and native platform generation/check first, then npm run sync-contract --prefix skills/common/plugins/openclaw-agent-observer to prepare publication runtime imports from the same committed contracts/agent-observability/v1/src. This original sync removes/recreates only its ignored src/generated/agent-observability target and copies canonical files; verify exact canonical file set/bytes. It is not an automatic hook of this platform command. Before any later clean native check, remove only an unchanged verified-owned generated copy after its consumers have stopped; never remove canonical Source or unrelated data. Separate staged successes do not establish simultaneous filesystem compatibility or successful execution of a containing docs:check/docs:publish-check/CI pipeline. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Child effects are cumulative, not rolled back if a later stage fails. Includes temporary mutation repositories and their known cleanup limitations, native publication/example checks, and migration cutover effects including Kubernetes cleanup. The direct docs-check program reads pages and Git source objects without writing. Current migration cutover selection does not invoke the separate container-build production build/push command; its real Kubernetes lease-cleanup effects remain. The platform child parses authenticated policy sources without executing runtime store/shell/SQL owners and compares policy plus full generated bytes; this does not add live cleanup or recovery. All existing cumulative effects, partial outputs, skips, external authority and STOP boundaries above remain. The selected local child-renderer closure includes LiteLLM configuration rendering and PostgreSQL recovery-manifest rendering; its imported volume preflight is not called because this producer does not pass --preflight. PostgreSQL service selection stages a versions.json-pinned chart in os.tmpdir()/kubeclaw-infrastructure-charts-<uid>, requiring a real owner-private directory. Existing archives are size/SHA/name/version/appVersion checked with tar; absent archives trigger curl HTTPS/OCI acquisition, bounded manifest/layer/digest checks and archive verification before rename into the retained cache. Helm performs an offline template/upgrade-view render with the local image post-renderer; the render-only password marker must not escape into resources, and reserved images must match pinned versions. It does not run PostgreSQL, backup SQL/shell or kubectl. Owned download-* directories are removed in finally; the private cache and verified archive remain, including after a later producer/check/mutation failure. Bad existing cache/archive, missing tools, network/acquisition, digest, archive identity, image or rendering failures stop; no automatic bad-cache repair or whole-cache rollback is promised. Thus --check compares normal outputs without writing them but is not filesystem-readonly or necessarily network-free. Repeated mutation calls can reuse/populate this separate cache; removing the owned mutation/Git fixture does not remove it. The rendered-policy helper receives these already acquired resources without starting tools or runtime owners. It selects one exact source/origin/kind/name/namespace, requires own-field paths and declared nested identities, and parses embedded registry ConfigMap YAML only as one valid unique-key/no-alias document. Missing/ambiguous resources or fields and identity changes stop. Values retain selected native resource provenance, conditional/fixture limits and outer Source authentication; declaration location is not misrepresented as selected-field offset. Original templates are not executed as arbitrary JavaScript or reimplemented by a scanner. The delegated platform producer performs the policy-only comparison Helm render described in Scope; normal child chart-cache/tool/network and failure effects already described remain in force. This adds no contract synchronization or runtime cleanup automatically. |
| Expected result and limits | All exact stages finish successfully in order; inspect the individual child outputs for their selected scope and any explicit skips. Limits: A successful aggregate retains every child limitation and skip. It does not establish live deployment, complete semantic correctness, or execution of examples merely read as data. |
| Owner | [documentation](../extend/documentation-maintenance.md) |
| When this changes | Changes to the listed receivers, their selected inputs or this command require this exact check and its named delegates. Documentation publication and reader-toolchain maintainers, with the explicitly delegated inventory and procedure owners must inspect complete diagnostics and partial effects, restore owned fixtures where applicable, and obtain independent review of the changed topic. Keep the declared environment, skips and STOP conditions; do not refresh expected data merely to hide a mismatch. Changes to producer revision/custody, either policy helper, supported selectors, actual store source/caller/default/cleanup authority, guidance family meaning/binding, selected template values, qualified contexts, explanation anchor or map identity require this exact producer/check plus its native policy source/custody tests and declared platform drift matrix. Inspect exact Source-derived values versus fallbacks/effective unknowns, refusal diagnostics, owned-fixture restoration and a meaningful reader cleanup/STOP decision; obtain independent affected-topic review. Commit actual Source before explicit current-revision generation; preserve the shared lock and unrelated outputs. Do not refresh mappings/baselines to conceal mismatch. Changes to conditional render recipe, selected origin/resource/nested identity, embedded YAML grammar or public provenance labels require the focused rendered-policy source tests plus the real native Job-TTL, embedded-registry and conditional-quarantine value projection/refusal/restoration controls. Preserve selected-profile absence and original surface arrays. Run original normal publication only after canonical contract synchronization; retain actual failed publication diagnostics until a genuine successful current successor exists. |

### npm-234: npm run typecheck:skills

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check TS erasable syntax/config discipline, source imports and registered source module paths. |
| Scope | Exact ordered command/delegate chain below; compiler/static/controlled local/direct-live boundaries remain distinct. |
| Environment and execution place | Invoke npm at repository root with prepared locked dependencies and required installed native tools. npm --prefix selects that package cwd/script and nested test chains. Root has no pre/post scripts; selected package lifecycle maps are explicit. Caller env/PATH/temp/Git configuration inherited except source-explicit child overrides.  |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | FIRST executes observer sync-contract (removes/replaces repository generated contract directory); then find, tsc --noEmit, Git and TypeScript transpile diagnostics. Thus not read-only despite typecheck name. Shell && stops at first nonzero; earlier writes/effects remain and are not rolled back as one transaction. A failed request/timeout is not absence of remote effects. |
| Expected result and limits | JSON configuration/source counts after assertions. Limits: No application tests or runtime behavior; source sync effects can precede later failure. The command description does not authorize a live operation or establish a fresh release/test result. |
| Owner | [plugin Foundation/SDK maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-sdk-or-shared-contracts) |
| When this changes | Changes to the listed receivers, their selected inputs or this command require this exact check and its named delegates. Runtime packaging, observer-contract synchronization and TypeScript configuration maintainers must inspect complete diagnostics and partial effects, restore owned fixtures where applicable, and obtain independent review of the changed topic. Keep the declared environment, skips and STOP conditions; do not refresh expected data merely to hide a mismatch. |

Underlying command definition. This is source data, not an instruction to run it.

```text
npm run typecheck:erasable
```
