### npm-235: npm run verify:plugin-system-v2

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check plugin-system contracts, builds, capability boundaries and local engine/isolation behavior. |
| Scope | Exact shell sequence starts with the OpenClaw agent-observer workspace build, then SDK check, temporary plugin builds, sandbox binary build, runtime typecheck, explicit contract programs, provider catalogue test, live-capability wrapper, and the local engine/recovery/isolation/installation/external-engine suffix. |
| Environment and execution place | Repository root with Node/npm dependencies, TypeScript and C compiler. Native isolation steps require a genuine delegated cgroup-v2 subtree in KUBECLAW_TEST_CGROUP_ROOT, plus supported Linux isolation facilities and built sandbox binary. The shell requires the variable when it reaches phase11; earlier build effects are not rolled back if it is missing. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | First build @kubeclaw/openclaw-agent-observer. Its syncContract deletes/replaces src/generated/agent-observability before compilation. TypeScript compiles into an owned temporary tree; success replaces the plugin dist directory. Finally removes compiler temporary output, not the synchronized source or successful dist. A compiler or later stage failure can therefore leave repository changes. The SDK alias checks bytes; plugin build emits into owned temporary output; sandbox build replaces its native binary. Local fixtures create and mutate plugin packages, state/effect/telemetry journals and owned Git/workspace trees. Checkpoint recovery deliberately SIGKILLs a child and invokes recovery CLI. Phase7 spawns a lock-holder process; security cases use injected capability callbacks, not real provider effects. Isolation invokes genuine restricted children. Several test trees are removed only at successful end. CURRENT STOP: verify:plugin-live-capabilities rejects demo-auth-smoke because its tests directory and required live-function.test.ts file are absent, before its package executions; this occurs after earlier aggregate steps, and prevents the following suffix from running. |
| Expected result and limits | Retain the first actual failed stage. On current source the live-capability wrapper has a declared incompatibility, so this command is not an assured green path. Later programs are intended only after that source incompatibility is resolved. Limits: Schema, fixture, local engine and isolation checks do not establish deployed provider or complete production workflow acceptance. No execution is inferred for a suffix skipped after failure. |
| Owner | [plugin Foundation/SDK maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-sdk-or-shared-contracts) |
| When this changes | Changes to the listed receivers, their selected inputs or this command require this exact check and its named delegates. Plugin-system SDK, registry, runtime isolation and engine maintainers must inspect complete diagnostics and partial effects, restore owned fixtures where applicable, and obtain independent review of the changed topic. Keep the declared environment, skips and STOP conditions; do not refresh expected data merely to hide a mismatch. |

### npm-236: npm run verify:contracts

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Run the ordered integration, checkpoint, test-gate, worker, observability and plugin contract checks. |
| Scope | Exact ordered child commands: typecheck:integration, knip:check, verify:test-gate:traceability, verify:test-gate:contracts, verify:test-gate:provider-registry, verify:test-gate:report-adapter-registry, verify:test-gate:report-adapter-runtime, verify:test-gate:junit-report-adapter, verify:test-gate:suite-resolver, verify:test-gate:plan-runner, verify:test-gate:remote-plan, verify:test-gate:remote-runtime, verify:test-gate:remote-import, verify:test-gate:legacy-retirement, verify:worker-core:contracts, verify:worker-core:attempt-executor, verify:worker-core:local-runtime, verify:worker-core:role-surfaces, verify:observability:legacy-cutover, plugin-system:inventory:check, verify:plugin-system-v2. Direct Node stages, if present, remain part of the exact command shown. |
| Environment and execution place | Run at the repository root with the combined prerequisites of the listed child commands. npm inherits the caller environment. The shell executes && stages in order and stops at the first nonzero result. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Child effects are cumulative, not rolled back if a later stage fails. Includes integration typechecks, knip, static checkpoint/scenario checks and exact test-gate/worker/observability delegates, followed by the plugin-system chain. Child effects include local runtimes, loopback endpoints, temporary durable stores and native isolation requirements. The current plugin live wrapper stops before its suffix. The delegated plugin-system chain starts with the observer workspace build: it synchronizes repository generated contract source before compiling and replaces observer dist on success; those outputs remain after a later failure. The selected provider-registry child creates an OS temporary `test-provider-registry-*` workspace and does not remove the workspace: successful execution retains the `unit` and invalid `bad-schema` package fixtures; failures may retain the earlier partial tree. Selected negative cases remove their own subdirectories only. Cleanup of other implementation/parity fixtures does not remove this separate workspace. Preserve diagnostics and identify the exact inactive owned path before cleanup. |
| Expected result and limits | All exact stages finish successfully in order; inspect the individual child outputs for their selected scope and any explicit skips. Limits: A successful aggregate retains every child limitation and skip. It does not establish live deployment, complete semantic correctness, or execution of examples merely read as data. |
| Owner | [Nova Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-nova-lifecycle-scheduling-or-run-authority); [Worker Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-worker-core-or-native-execution); [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import); [plugin Foundation/SDK maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-sdk-or-shared-contracts); [documentation](../extend/documentation-maintenance.md) |
| When this changes | Changes to the listed receivers, their selected inputs or this command require this exact check and its named delegates. Nova integration and contract maintainers, together with each explicit worker, observability, plugin and documentation delegate must inspect complete diagnostics and partial effects, restore owned fixtures where applicable, and obtain independent review of the changed topic. Keep the declared environment, skips and STOP conditions; do not refresh expected data merely to hide a mismatch. |

### npm-238: npm run verify:product

| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Run skill typechecks, scaffold typechecks, contracts, plugin pipeline checks and documentation checks. |
| Scope | Exact ordered child commands: typecheck:skills, progress:scaffold:typecheck, verify:contracts, verify:pipeline, docs:check. Direct Node stages, if present, remain part of the exact command shown. Delegated platform-inventory checking also derives typed store-policy declarations and source/caller joins; its alias is not store-only. Platform policy acquisition also uses the existing selected native Helm/static resources and one separate policy-only Prism ingestion comparison, labelled helm:prism-ingestion-policy: ingestion.enabled is enabled with a typed boolean override, explicit render-only CPU/memory sizing and the existing native-worker fixture settings. The maintained selected Prism profile still disables ingestion. This comparison supplies only policy selection and is never merged into the original selected resource/signal/endpoint arrays; it is not a deployment, inferred default or observed capacity. |
| Environment and execution place | Run at the repository root with the combined prerequisites of the listed child commands. npm inherits the caller environment. The shell executes && stages in order and stops at the first nonzero result. The platform child selects its existing inventory sourceRevision before the shared-lock fallback, verifies cited producer/authority bytes, and does not silently select HEAD or update the shared lock. Optional explicit current-HEAD source-first generation is a separate producer invocation, not an automatic aggregate action. The selected static PostgreSQL renderer also requires tar and a private writable OS temporary chart cache. A matching cached archive is reverified; a cache miss requires curl and HTTPS access to the locked chart transport (the selected PostgreSQL lock uses immutable Docker Hub OCI manifest/layer acquisition; supported HTTPS archive locks use direct HTTPS). Node parses Go source statically; these direct platform commands do not invoke a Go binary. Other aggregate/CI delegates retain their separately declared Go/tool prerequisites. Native source custody and normal publication require distinct preparation states. The supported maintenance sequence is clean committed Source and native platform generation/check first, then npm run sync-contract --prefix skills/common/plugins/openclaw-agent-observer to prepare publication runtime imports from the same committed contracts/agent-observability/v1/src. This original sync removes/recreates only its ignored src/generated/agent-observability target and copies canonical files; verify exact canonical file set/bytes. It is not an automatic hook of this platform command. Before any later clean native check, remove only an unchanged verified-owned generated copy after its consumers have stopped; never remove canonical Source or unrelated data. Separate staged successes do not establish simultaneous filesystem compatibility or successful execution of a containing docs:check/docs:publish-check/CI pipeline. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Child effects are cumulative, not rolled back if a later stage fails. The skill typecheck synchronizes generated observer contracts before checking. Subsequent contract/plugin/documentation aggregates retain all local writes, native prerequisites and current source incompatibilities. A failed stage stops later stages; earlier output remains. The delegated plugin-system chain starts with the observer workspace build: it synchronizes repository generated contract source before compiling and replaces observer dist on success; those outputs remain after a later failure. The selected provider-registry child creates an OS temporary `test-provider-registry-*` workspace and does not remove the workspace: successful execution retains the `unit` and invalid `bad-schema` package fixtures; failures may retain the earlier partial tree. Selected negative cases remove their own subdirectories only. Cleanup of other implementation/parity fixtures does not remove this separate workspace. Preserve diagnostics and identify the exact inactive owned path before cleanup. The platform child parses authenticated policy sources without executing runtime store/shell/SQL owners and compares policy plus full generated bytes; this does not add live cleanup or recovery. All existing cumulative effects, partial outputs, skips, external authority and STOP boundaries above remain. The selected local child-renderer closure includes LiteLLM configuration rendering and PostgreSQL recovery-manifest rendering; its imported volume preflight is not called because this producer does not pass --preflight. PostgreSQL service selection stages a versions.json-pinned chart in os.tmpdir()/kubeclaw-infrastructure-charts-<uid>, requiring a real owner-private directory. Existing archives are size/SHA/name/version/appVersion checked with tar; absent archives trigger curl HTTPS/OCI acquisition, bounded manifest/layer/digest checks and archive verification before rename into the retained cache. Helm performs an offline template/upgrade-view render with the local image post-renderer; the render-only password marker must not escape into resources, and reserved images must match pinned versions. It does not run PostgreSQL, backup SQL/shell or kubectl. Owned download-* directories are removed in finally; the private cache and verified archive remain, including after a later producer/check/mutation failure. Bad existing cache/archive, missing tools, network/acquisition, digest, archive identity, image or rendering failures stop; no automatic bad-cache repair or whole-cache rollback is promised. Thus --check compares normal outputs without writing them but is not filesystem-readonly or necessarily network-free. Repeated mutation calls can reuse/populate this separate cache; removing the owned mutation/Git fixture does not remove it. The rendered-policy helper receives these already acquired resources without starting tools or runtime owners. It selects one exact source/origin/kind/name/namespace, requires own-field paths and declared nested identities, and parses embedded registry ConfigMap YAML only as one valid unique-key/no-alias document. Missing/ambiguous resources or fields and identity changes stop. Values retain selected native resource provenance, conditional/fixture limits and outer Source authentication; declaration location is not misrepresented as selected-field offset. Original templates are not executed as arbitrary JavaScript or reimplemented by a scanner. The delegated platform producer performs the policy-only comparison Helm render described in Scope; normal child chart-cache/tool/network and failure effects already described remain in force. This adds no contract synchronization or runtime cleanup automatically. |
| Expected result and limits | All exact stages finish successfully in order; inspect the individual child outputs for their selected scope and any explicit skips. Limits: A successful aggregate retains every child limitation and skip. It does not establish live deployment, complete semantic correctness, or execution of examples merely read as data. |
| Owner | [Nova Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-nova-lifecycle-scheduling-or-run-authority); [Worker Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-worker-core-or-native-execution); [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import); [plugin Foundation/SDK maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-sdk-or-shared-contracts); [documentation](../extend/documentation-maintenance.md) |
| When this changes | Changes to the listed receivers, their selected inputs or this command require this exact check and its named delegates. Nova integration and contract maintainers, together with each explicit worker, observability, plugin and documentation delegate must inspect complete diagnostics and partial effects, restore owned fixtures where applicable, and obtain independent review of the changed topic. Keep the declared environment, skips and STOP conditions; do not refresh expected data merely to hide a mismatch. Changes to producer revision/custody, either policy helper, supported selectors, actual store source/caller/default/cleanup authority, guidance family meaning/binding, selected template values, qualified contexts, explanation anchor or map identity require this exact producer/check plus its native policy source/custody tests and declared platform drift matrix. Inspect exact Source-derived values versus fallbacks/effective unknowns, refusal diagnostics, owned-fixture restoration and a meaningful reader cleanup/STOP decision; obtain independent affected-topic review. Commit actual Source before explicit current-revision generation; preserve the shared lock and unrelated outputs. Do not refresh mappings/baselines to conceal mismatch. Changes to conditional render recipe, selected origin/resource/nested identity, embedded YAML grammar or public provenance labels require the focused rendered-policy source tests plus the real native Job-TTL, embedded-registry and conditional-quarantine value projection/refusal/restoration controls. Preserve selected-profile absence and original surface arrays. Run original normal publication only after canonical contract synchronization; retain actual failed publication diagnostics until a genuine successful current successor exists. |

Underlying command definition. This is source data, not an instruction to run it.

```text
npm run typecheck:skills && npm run progress:scaffold:typecheck && npm run verify:contracts && npm run verify:pipeline && npm run docs:check
```

### npm-239: npm run progress:scaffold:typecheck

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Type-check progress scaffold tooling with noEmit. |
| Scope | Exact tools/**/*.ts plus imported dependency declarations under project_setup tsconfig extending root strict/erasable NodeNext config. |
| Environment and execution place | Repository root via npm, installed locked Node/TypeScript dependencies and full source/configuration records; no root npm pre/post definitions. Installed tsc/Node types. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Compiler diagnostics only; no running scaffold/program/project or writing progress/pipeline. Actual configs have no incremental build cache enabled. |
| Expected result and limits | tsc exits 0 (normally no output), otherwise diagnostics. Limits: No actual scaffold validation of a selected project, runtime graph execution or persistence. |
| Owner | [Nova Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-nova-lifecycle-scheduling-or-run-authority) |
| When this changes | Changes to the listed receivers, their selected inputs or this command require this exact check and its named delegates. Project progress-scaffold and Nova project-input maintainers must inspect complete diagnostics and partial effects, restore owned fixtures where applicable, and obtain independent review of the changed topic. Keep the declared environment, skips and STOP conditions; do not refresh expected data merely to hide a mismatch. |

### npm-240: npm run progress:scaffold

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Create a project progress scaffold, or explicitly validate/publish/print selected pair with forwarded flags. |
| Scope | Bare npm command passes no required --project/--swarm, so exits 1; user must pass npm -- --project NAME or --swarm PATH. Defaults nearest.git/repo, Projects/name/src/.swarm/progress.scaffold.json. Default discovery writes scaffold; --apply converts validated scaffold into paired progress/pipeline; --check reads/converts only; --print prints only. |
| Environment and execution place | Repository root via npm, installed locked Node/TypeScript dependencies and full source/configuration records; no root npm pre/post definitions. Complete selected .swarm/retained published pair, project descriptions/module state; --repo/--swarm/--scaffold choose actual filesystem targets. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Default writes scaffold then prints diagnostics and next step (zero does not imply TODO diagnostics resolved). --apply validates first then publishJsonPair into selected swarm; ownership/pair generation follows real foundation publisher. --check/print no pair writes. No project/test/provider execution. Publication error retains original pair/transaction boundaries; do not claim arbitrary path confinement or live atomic recovery. |
| Expected result and limits | Default wrote scaffold+diagnostics; apply wrote progress.json/pipeline.json; check passed; print JSON pair; missing target/invalid scaffold exits 1. Limits: Not actual executed pipeline/provider graph, complete production-ready TODOs, generic migration or deployed progress. |
| Owner | [Nova Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-nova-lifecycle-scheduling-or-run-authority) |
| When this changes | Changes to the listed receivers, their selected inputs or this command require this exact check and its named delegates. Project progress-scaffold and Nova project-input maintainers must inspect complete diagnostics and partial effects, restore owned fixtures where applicable, and obtain independent review of the changed topic. Keep the declared environment, skips and STOP conditions; do not refresh expected data merely to hide a mismatch. |

node skills/nova/project_setup/tools/progress-scaffold.ts

### npm-241: npm run verify:prism:runtime-role

| Scope | Actual roles/ownership/external capabilities/plugins/extensions/entrypoints; optional paired additional-plugin and role-addition test inputs; Prism must select worker-core and prism-engine, but no Nova or Buster packages. |

| Authority, writes and remaining state | Local JSON and filesystem assertions only; no package installation, runtime import/activation, cluster requests or file writes. |
| Expected result and limits | Two JSON ok summaries, the first failure prevents later &&. Limits: No actual capability grant, packed runtime execution or protocol compatibility. |
| Owner | [Prism maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-prism-contracts-services-data-or-engine); [platform deployment maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-charts-or-gitops) |

Runtime packaging and Prism role-definition maintainers must inspect the full diagnostics, partial effects, declared skips and cleanup results and obtain independent topic review. A command reference does not authorize a live target or establish a new execution result. |

### npm-248: npm run verify:prism:buster-fidelity:live

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Run real destructive Prism restart/backup/restore-job checks then compare supplied Buster defect/corrected results. |
| Scope | Same19 line source for buster-fidelity:live/recovery:live/e2e:real:prism:failures; worker Pod delete/rollout,PostgreSQL Pod delete/rollout,backup Job and restore-proof Job wait, preexisting two Buster result files. |
| Environment and execution place | PRISM_NAMESPACE required, kubectl on PATH/current authorized cluster credentials; PRISM_BUSTER_DEFECT_RESULT_FILE and CORRECTED_RESULT_FILE required when reached. Needs matching workload selectors/controllers/cronjobs and permission for deletions/jobs; no synthetic local mode. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Deletes selected actual worker/Postgres Pods --wait=false, waits deployments/statefulset10m, creates timestamped backup and restore-proof Jobs then waits15m each. Reads result files after mutations. No Buster invocation, no finally/cleanup of created Jobs, no selected-cluster explicit safety check inside this receiver; preserve/inspect jobs and resource identities on error. |
| Expected result and limits | A passed prism-live-failures.v2 JSON report with restart, backup and supplied-result checks. The two supplied Buster result files must have equal baseline identities, the expected visual/accessibility failures in the defective result, and passing corresponding corrected results. Limits: Does not itself execute Buster, prove all failures/restore semantics or remove created jobs; no source-level authorization inferred from name. |
| Owner | [Prism maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-prism-contracts-services-data-or-engine); [platform deployment maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-charts-or-gitops) |
| When this changes | Changes to the listed native receivers or selected inputs require this exact command and its named delegates. A command reference does not authorize a live target or establish a new execution result. |

### npm-256: npm run verify:reliability:contracts

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check local recovery, lifecycle, remote-result import and Git workspace contracts. |
| Scope | Five serial contract programs followed by the Git-workspace package boundary, functional and sync-disposition tests. |
| Environment and execution place | Repository root with installed Node workspace dependencies, /usr/bin/git, /usr/bin/env and shell utilities. npm changes execution directory for the Git-workspace package tests. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Creates local state, artifact and telemetry stores, temporary Git repositories, branches and worktrees. A checkpoint child is deliberately SIGKILLed and recovered through the real CLI. Git fetch/push targets a local bare repository; fake Git programs test output, timeout, cancellation and shutdown. The remote importer receives synthetic signed result fixtures through in-process callbacks, not an external Buster service. Most owned trees have finally cleanup; the Git live-function program removes its tree only at its successful end, so an earlier error can leave it. KEEP_TEST_TMP retains importer fixtures. |
| Expected result and limits | Each serial child finishes its assertions and exits zero, including rejection, idempotence and recovery cases. Limits: No deployed recovery, real remote test execution, external Git remote or production authorization is established by these local fixtures. |
| Owner | [Nova Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-nova-lifecycle-scheduling-or-run-authority); [Worker Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-worker-core-or-native-execution); [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import); [telemetry and source-component maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-telemetry-or-derived-views); [plugin Foundation/SDK maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-sdk-or-shared-contracts) |

### npm-257: npm run verify:reliability

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Run the complete local reliability regression glob, then recovery/import and Git-workspace contract checks. |
| Scope | All current reliability *.test.mts and *.test.mjs files selected by the shell, followed in && order by five explicit contract programs and the Git-workspace workspace tests. The exact selected file vector is retained in sourceEvidence; it includes native worker, Redis, local runtime/effect recovery, Buster storage, coverage, evidence and SDK regressions. |
| Environment and execution place | Repository root with installed Node/npm workspace dependencies, /usr/bin/git, tar, mkfifo, flock, /usr/bin/python3, shell utilities and a C compiler. REDIS_SERVER and REDIS_SOURCE_SERVER must point to authentic native Redis binaries with adjacent redis-cli/check-rdb tools; no emulator or automatic skip is supplied. Native observations require readable Linux cgroup-v2 counters, /proc and trusted /etc/machine-id; native startup/trust tests depend on the actual privilege/ownership environment. Locale-sensitive SDK cases retain their declared locale requirements. ARCHVIEWER_TEST_NGINX and openssl must be real installed tools. Selected tests require actual kubectl and Helm. Helm may use HTTPS or immutable OCI pulls and a private verified infrastructure-chart cache. One independent projection case waits a real minute; there is no fast-clock substitution. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Runs real local child processes, intentional SIGKILL and cancellation, CPU workloads, loopback HTTP/TCP services, temporary Git histories/worktrees, tar archives, file journals, artifact/record/blob stores and FIFO/symlink negative fixtures. Redis cases start, stop and restart native loopback servers, change their local capacity policy and migrate an owned snapshot through the actual offline migration script. The Lighthouse startup case deliberately runs Node as Chrome and expects launch rejection. Runtime-dispatch and Discord/operator endpoints are controlled loopback protocol peers, not real gateway/model/Discord services. Forge fixtures execute native file operations and ESLint in local worktrees. Most tests have finally/after cleanup, but some fixtures finish setup before the caller can register cleanup; an early setup error can leave owned resources. KEEP_TEST_TMP may retain import fixtures. Test timeouts and cleanup deadlines vary by file; there is no single aggregate child timeout or transaction rollback. Archviewer starts native nginx on private loopback. Tailscale/exposure tests invoke actual kubectl against a generated loopback Kubernetes wire-protocol fixture, not a cluster controller or tailnet. Stateful chart checks can fetch authenticated OCI/HTTPS chart data and retain verified cache archives; rendering does not apply resources. Historical CLI diagnostics temporarily write unique receiver-adjacent source files and remove them in finally; early setup failures before that region can leave staged files. Proxy audit uses original adapters with a controlled loopback HTTP peer. Retention fixtures mutate and corrupt only their own local stores, use real locks and SIGKILL, and restore or remove owned trees according to each hook. KEEP_PROJECTION_TMP and explicit proof-output variables can retain fixtures or proof files. Archived proofs read by tests are fixture inputs, not fresh production observations. |
| Expected result and limits | Every selected Node test and subsequent serial contract stage passes its stated positive/negative assertions. Missing native prerequisites fail rather than silently substituting a simulation. Inspect explicit skipped provider nodes: a native skipped plan can validate terminal-store behavior without executing a provider. Limits: Local crash, protocol, filesystem and kernel-observation regressions do not establish deployed recovery, isolated production attribution, live model/gateway/Discord operation, cluster restoration, or full provider acceptance. Child exit zero does not erase retained files or prove cleanup beyond each actual assertion. |

### npm-258: npm run versions:sync

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Synchronize version-derived tracked inputs and dependency/tool locks in declared && order. |
| Scope | versions.json drives Docker build ARGs, chart/images/plugin versions, selected infrastructure/bootstrap/workflow settings, Python input requirements/Go requirements and ops-tool inventory, then Codex lock, then runtime tool locks. |
| Environment and execution place | Repository root via npm, installed locked Node/TypeScript dependencies and full source/configuration records; no root npm pre/post definitions. Requires npm, uv, exact manifest-selected local Go toolchain, registry/PyPI/module network as needed; inherits configured caches/proxies/credentials. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | First versions writes all validated changed targets. Next Codex lock on drift runs npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund in ops/pod. Finally runtime update may uv compile hashed x86_64/aarch64 Python3.11 locks using PyPI and go get -tool/mod tidy/download/verify with GOTOOLCHAIN=local;600-second child timeout. Private temporary constraint directory cleaned; tracked outputs/cache/network may change. Failed later step does not rollback earlier tracked changes; receipt published only after successful resolutions. |
| Expected result and limits | Per-step JSON changed paths/version/lock input-output counts; fail stops later && commands. Limits: Not build/image signature/deployed compatibility or successful live rollout; no atomic all-files transaction. Review partial version/lock changes before retry. |
| Owner | [Release/deployment maintainer](../extend/developer-handbook.md#route-each-source-change-to-its-documentation-owner) |
| When this changes | Changes to the listed receivers, their selected inputs or this command require this exact check and its named delegates. Version manifest, Codex package-lock and runtime-toolchain lock maintainers must inspect complete diagnostics and partial effects, restore owned fixtures where applicable, and obtain independent review of the changed topic. Keep the declared environment, skips and STOP conditions; do not refresh expected data merely to hide a mismatch. |

Underlying command definition. This is source data, not an instruction to run it.

```text
node scripts/versions.mjs --write && node scripts/sync-codex-lock.mjs --write && node scripts/runtime-tool-locks.mjs --update
```

- [package.json](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ea887c6daacde7f94ed61ee89837bf393e7436df/package.json)

- [scripts/sync-codex-lock.mjs](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ea887c6daacde7f94ed61ee89837bf393e7436df/scripts/sync-codex-lock.mjs)

### npm-259: npm run versions:check

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check version-derived fields and Codex package lock without updating. |
| Scope | versions --check first compares derived outputs then validates runtime-tool-lock receipt input/output hashes and Python root pins; second sync-codex-lock --check validates declared/resolved Codex dependency. |
| Environment and execution place | Repository root via npm, installed locked Node/TypeScript dependencies and full source/configuration records; no root npm pre/post definitions. Complete versions/chart/template/lock inputs. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Read-only source/lock comparisons, no npm install/uv/go network path selected. Exceptions nonzero and && prevents next check. |
| Expected result and limits | JSON checked/changed(empty), runtime lock counts, then unchanged Codex version JSON. Limits: No new provenance/signature/runtime compatibility or live acceptance from pinned strings/hashes. |
| Owner | [Release/deployment maintainer](../extend/developer-handbook.md#route-each-source-change-to-its-documentation-owner) |
| When this changes | Changes to the listed receivers, their selected inputs or this command require this exact check and its named delegates. Version manifest, Codex package-lock and runtime-toolchain lock maintainers must inspect complete diagnostics and partial effects, restore owned fixtures where applicable, and obtain independent review of the changed topic. Keep the declared environment, skips and STOP conditions; do not refresh expected data merely to hide a mismatch. |

Underlying command definition. This is source data, not an instruction to run it.

```text
node scripts/versions.mjs --check && node scripts/sync-codex-lock.mjs --check
```

Limits: Historical failure reproduction, synthetic protocol acceptance or successor schema/type checks do not establish a live model, gateway, provider, restored production run or whole release acceptance. |

### npm-266: npm run verify:worker-core:native-runtime

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Test native-worker startup, launcher and rendering contracts, then run the Go NRI race suite. |
| Scope | Four explicit Node test files followed by the exact GOTOOLCHAIN=local Go test command in tools/native-worker-nri, with readonly modules, race detection and no result caching. These use real Go NRI protocol inputs, not an installed containerd runtime. |
| Environment and execution place | Repository root through npm, installed locked native tools/dependencies and actual tracked inputs/Git objects. No root pre/post script definitions observed. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Requires Linux /proc, /etc/machine-id, a C compiler, systemd-analyze, Helm, the selected Go toolchain and the tested root-owned policy boundaries. Tests compile temporary C/Go binaries, build Node bundles, create chmod/symlink negative fixtures and invoke native-worker CLI refusal cases. NRI helpers verify the Go version and modules before readonly builds. Go build/test caches and module downloads can change: readonly modules do not prohibit network access. Finally blocks remove owned temporary files; this command does not activate host systemd services or deploy a cluster. |
| Expected result and limits | The selected Node tests and fresh verbose Go race tests all pass. Missing tools, wrong versions or insufficient root/host authority fail rather than stand in for a successful native case. Limits: No successful kernel-pool admission, containerd NRI installation, deployed cluster workload or live Pod capacity follows from these tests. |
| Owner | [Worker Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-worker-core-or-native-execution) |

### npm-267: npm run verify:prism:native-dispatch

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Test the native PostgreSQL operation journal, then durable handling of a refused HTTP dispatch. |
| Scope | The first child requires a loopback administrative URL for an empty disposable server. The second requires the separate prism_runtime runtime URL and prism database. The tests perform real bootstrap, migrations, eight-way SQL concurrency, writer SIGKILL, immutable-identity and journal-negative cases. |
| Environment and execution place | Repository root through npm, installed locked native tools/dependencies and actual tracked inputs/Git objects. No root pre/post script definitions observed. Set PRISM_NATIVE_OPERATION_TEST_ADMIN_URL to an empty disposable loopback PostgreSQL server for the first child. Set PRISM_NATIVE_OPERATION_TEST_DATABASE_URL to that server’s migrated prism database using prism_runtime for the second child. The first child leaves database/roles/state for the later check; neither child drops them. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Creates an actual prism database, roles, schema and rows and starts a writer that is deliberately killed. Pools and owned local temporary files are cleaned, but database roles, rows and the database itself are not dropped. The second child reserves then closes a loopback port, observes an actual HTTP connection refusal and checks durable SQL records. The shell stops after a failed first child. Use only the intended disposable database and inspect partial database state before retry. |
| Expected result and limits | Native Node TAP/assertion results; selected tests must pass, failures nonzero. Skips where declared remain skips, not proof. Limits: A zero exit does not establish worker completion, a positive native-kernel path, production database safety or database cleanup. |
| Owner | [Prism maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-prism-contracts-services-data-or-engine) |
| When this changes | Changes to the listed receivers, their selected inputs or this command require this exact check and its named delegates. Prism PostgreSQL operation-journal and dispatch-adapter maintainers must inspect complete diagnostics and partial effects, restore owned fixtures where applicable, and obtain independent review of the changed topic. Keep the declared environment, skips and STOP conditions; do not refresh expected data merely to hide a mismatch. |

## Guide-Owned Verification Routes

These 18 supported forms belong to the linked complete guides rather than root npm aliases. Preparation, execution, verification and cleanup remain separate duties. Delegated helpers are not independent public routes.

### guide-1: node docs/site/use/workflows/examples/first-project.mjs "$FIRST_PROJECT"

Follow the [complete guide procedure](../use/workflows/README.md#materialize-and-compile-a-first-project).

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Materialize and deterministically compile one first-project example. |
| Scope | An eight-stage nova-project.v2 graph and two resolved direct-command test plans; compilation does not run those plans or activate a platform. |
| Environment and execution place | Use the canonical selected clean checkout and locked development dependencies, Node 24 and Git. Supply one new normalized absolute directory, not /; an existing destination is rejected. The later lint policy is an operator-selected path, not a generated valid live policy. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Create the destination, repository/workspace directories, example source/test files, a local Git baseline commit, project.json and compiled.json. Partial setup remains if a later operation fails; no provider, cluster, model, or adapter activation is selected. |
| Expected result and limits | compiled-example JSON has execution=false, platformAdmission=false, eight stages and a definition digest. The greeting source already returns hello; the separate node --test example checks that fixture, not an implemented project journey. |
| Owner | [Nova Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-nova-lifecycle-scheduling-or-run-authority) |
| When this changes | Change the helper, compiler/encoding, test-plan coverage or declared fixture together; check deterministic graph and provider-plan inputs, and keep this compile-only procedure distinct from actual execution. |

### guide-2: node docs/site/use/workflows/examples/local-core.mjs prepare "$LOCAL_CORE"

Follow the [complete guide procedure](../use/workflows/local-core.md#1-materialize-the-complete-inputs).

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Create the owned local Core journey inputs. |
| Scope | A disposable Git repository, one successful Delivery Lint graph, one invalid-path graph, denied-grant platform, artifact/telemetry stores and source marker. |
| Environment and execution place | Use Node 24, installed development dependencies, Git, GNU util-linux /usr/bin/flock with --timeout, and a local filesystem qualified for locking/append/fsync. Supply the normalized absolute owned fixture path. No model/service credential, cluster, Redis, browser, Docker, Go or external provider is selected. The destination must not exist; existing ancestors must be directories, not symlinks. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Write private fixture source/configuration and commit a local Git baseline. Store source revision and owned-root marker; do not run a stage. A failure can leave a partial owned directory. |
| Expected result and limits | prepared JSON has execution=false and next=run. This is input preparation, not platform or runtime acceptance. |
| Owner | [Nova Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-nova-lifecycle-scheduling-or-run-authority) |
| When this changes | Change the helper, Delivery Lint/repository/artifact/telemetry contracts, Core CLI admission, or retained-evidence verifier together; use the canonical prepare/run/verify procedure and inspect the exact failure. Do not weaken grants or edit preserved state to match expectations. |

| Expected result and limits | verified-local-core-journey requires succeeded and blocked outcomes, delivery_lint.path_invalid, grant rejection, original artifact byte/digest/producer agreement, journal/audit heads and same-run telemetry. It is not a project compiler, remote Buster/provider, cluster, Redis or human acceptance. |

### guide-15: node scripts/lint-baseline-prune.mjs --report artifacts/lint-report.json --baseline charts/kubeclaw/files/config/lint-baseline.json

Follow the [complete guide procedure](../extend/lint.md#remove-resolved-debt).

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check whether the current full lint report still observes every recorded baseline fingerprint. |
| Scope | Compare the selected baseline with one full debt-visible report bound to its exact bytes; this is not a new analyser run or a fresh application lint result. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the repository root with a supported Node runtime and read access to the selected report and baseline. The helper uses Node built-ins; it does not run analysers or fetch a database. Before this step, produce a complete unscoped full-tier report with includeDebt=true, current baseline digest, zero changed-file scope and successful complete findings for every baseline tool. Use the canonical target-image/pinned-tool lint-report procedure to produce that input. Stop on any digest, scope, debt visibility, tool status, JSON or file error. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Read and parse the selected report and baseline and compute the candidate retained groups in memory. Without --write the helper does not change the baseline, create output files or execute child tools. It does not authenticate a reviewer or grant approval to remove debt. |
| Expected result and limits | Zero prints lint baseline is fresh only when no fingerprints would be removed. Stale entries throw a nonzero diagnostic giving the count and --write direction. That exact stale diagnostic permits preparing a reviewed candidate, not deletion approval; any other error is STOP. No passing application, calendar/approval or live-operation result follows from this check. |
| Owner | [Lint maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#run-lint-for-a-selected-source-change) |
| When this changes | Changes to report/baseline schema, digest binding, tool findings, stale-entry selection, approval fields or either helper require the full lint procedure and focused helper checks. Keep original reports, exact baseline diffs and failure diagnostics. Do not turn a stale-count message into approval or change a failed report to match the desired baseline. |

## Package and Specialist Check Routes

These procedure routes complement the explicit commands above. They retain package-specific and focused native checks; root aliases do not replace their actual prerequisites, effects or proof limits. A route is not a claim that every private helper is an independent public command.

### route-1: Package-local checks and focused package subtests

Follow the [complete guide procedure](../extend/plugin-catalogue/README.md).

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Select the actual installed package check through its catalogue entry and shared host/testing procedure. |
| Scope | All49 actual common/Nova/Buster wrapper-selected packages have explicit per-package npm test lifecycle entries below, including exact cwd/hooks/nested behavior and seven duties. The root verify:plugin-packages aggregate (npm-45) retains discovery/ordering/inherited authority and its own limits; it is not independent certification of every package algorithm. Prism and Ops MCP catalogue commands retain their separate native command responsibilities; the Prism registration-only direct test is guide-18, not the full Prism package. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository root with its locked Node dependencies. Start with the package page, then extend/testing.md and extend/host-and-engine.md. Install that package’s declared dependencies/native tools and provide only its selected fixture authority. An absent command is not an invitation to invent npm test; do not use a historical catalogue success as current preparation. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | npm test --prefix `<actual-package-directory>` executes that package’s pretest/test/posttest with caller authority. Directly named subtests execute only the named body, not the full lifecycle. Package tests are not sandboxed or universally read-only; retain their actual fixture/cache/generated-file effects and cleanup limits. The root wrapper’s observer build and review hooks remain real writes. |
| Expected result and limits | Require the exact selected child assertions and terminal result, not only file discovery, registration import or a dated result. The catalogue’s local results do not establish current host/cluster availability. Follow the package source and shared proof ladder for a real function, boundary and target-host exercise. |
| Owner | [Selected package/source-component maintainer](../extend/developer-handbook.md#route-each-source-change-to-its-documentation-owner); [plugin Foundation/SDK maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-sdk-or-shared-contracts). Resolve the package maintainer through the selected catalogue page and source component. |
| When this changes | Changes to the selected package manifest, script lifecycle, package source contract, host registration or a directly documented focused test select the exact focused commands named in this entry’s Scope and its canonical procedure. Run the complete selected lifecycle or ordered chain, not an arbitrary passing subtest. Preserve the first diagnostic and any partial state; repair the actual owning input/tool and re-run the affected control. This focused result does not replace broader release or live acceptance. |

### route-16: Buster error and provider reference generation

Follow the [complete guide procedure](../reference/buster-error-codes.md#maintenance-rule).

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Maintain the two bounded Buster references through their actual native owners. |
| Scope | node scripts/generate-buster-error-reference.mjs and node scripts/generate-buster-provider-reference.mjs compare by default; --write selects their one tracked page. Error --describe-discovery emits its bounded discovery declaration after analysis. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository root with its locked Node dependencies. Requires installed TypeScript for error analysis, complete declared Buster inputs and supported Node. Error revision is selected by --revision=<40-hex> or recorded page revision and format-checked, not a Git-byte proof. Provider generation separately requires Git and exact current/selected-commit bytes for its manifests, schemas, catalogue/parser/template and generator; commit those sources first. The provider-reference maintenance procedure requires a clean repository checkout before generation or `--write`. Stop if tracked inputs or the target page have unrelated edits; retain the exact original page/diff and first failure rather than overwriting another change. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Error generation recursively reads its bounded engine/plugin source set and builds output without running providers. Provider generation reads exact local Git objects and schema/catalogue inputs. Each --write replaces only its reference page; comparison does not rewrite it. Neither starts remote providers/services or applies resources. |
| Expected result and limits | Require the native exact-freshness assertions. A stale output needs reviewed regeneration; an analysis/count/pin failure needs source qualification, not edited expected counts/digests. Error-link formatting alone does not certify that historical links equal current inputs; provider pin equality is still not runtime/remote health. |
| Owner | [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import); [documentation](../extend/documentation-maintenance.md) |
| When this changes | Changes to native Buster error definitions or provider registration/configuration schemas select their corresponding generator, not arbitrary CLI syntax. Follow [error-reference maintenance](buster-error-codes.md#maintenance-rule) and [provider-reference maintenance](buster-provider-configuration.md#maintenance-rule): change the real implementation first, qualify its source, run the matching default check, review exact generated diffs for an intentional write and repeat the check. Preserve first failures and never edit generated rows to hide source drift. |

### route-79: npm test --prefix skills/nova/plugins/review

Follow the [complete guide procedure](../extend/plugin-catalogue/kubeclaw.review.md).

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check review protocol, policy, budgets, source/evidence identity, reduction, verification, repository audit/revalidation and report encoding/storage contracts, including local Core/Git/HTTP integration. |
| Scope | npm test runs pretest audit/revalidation contracts, the ordered main suite (cluster contracts and schema checks first), coverage checks, then posttest report-encoding and a second portable live-function run. Native HTTP fixtures return deterministic review/verifier responses; they do not call a real model or prove review quality on production source. The complete selected npm script declarations appear in the read-only definition below. npm --prefix starts at the package cwd; explicit cd/nested scripts preserve their native execution places. No absent hook is assumed. |
| Environment and execution place | Use npm test --prefix skills/nova/plugins/review with installed workspace dependencies (including Ajv and tokenizer packages), TypeScript-capable Node, Git, writable temporary storage and loopback ports. Locale children require Node ICU support for the selected en-US/da-DK/tr-TR/sv-SE locales and set LANG/LC_ALL while removing NODE_TEST_CONTEXT. The live fixture sets and then deletes KUBECLAW_REVIEW_TEST_TOKEN in its child process. No production gateway/model credential is required by the inspected local harness. GNU-compatible `/usr/bin/flock` supporting `--exclusive --timeout`, executable `/bin/sh` and `/bin/cat`, and a compatible file-lock/durability filesystem are required by actual durable-store readiness/read/write. Missing or incompatible lock utility blocks this check. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Creates temporary Git histories, journals, durable records/blobs, effect/lock stores and local HTTP/TCP servers, including a TCP endpoint that intentionally destroys connections to exercise uncertain dispatch. Locale tests spawn Node children, persist and truncate exact owned journal prefixes, write report/summary evidence and materialize current/historical source overlays with node_modules symlinks. Schema commands are invoked with --check and compare generated text without rewriting schemas. Finally blocks close adapters/servers and remove owned roots; they are not a transaction covering interruption or every subprocess before finally. Actual durable-store operations create lock/store state and spawn the native flock-to-sh/cat lock-holder; release is awaited. Lock/start/unlock failure remains a test failure, not a skip. |
| Expected result and limits | Every pretest/main/posttest command must exit zero. Main && failures stop later main commands, and a failed test prevents successful lifecycle completion. Expected blocked, retry and reconciliation-required cases must remain expected negatives, not successful external review. TAP and per-suite summaries are local test outcomes; live-function explicitly reports nativeGatewayOrModelProof:false. |
| Owner | [Nova Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-nova-lifecycle-scheduling-or-run-authority); [Selected package/source-component maintainer](../extend/developer-handbook.md#route-each-source-change-to-its-documentation-owner); [plugin Foundation/SDK maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-sdk-or-shared-contracts) |
| When this changes | Run this package test after review source/policy/protocol, schema, verification, storage, governor, repository-audit or encoding changes. Run npm run schema:check --prefix skills/nova/plugins/review for the narrow generated-schema check; schema:generate is a separate writing command, not selected by npm test. Run the package build separately for TypeScript and retain native uncertainty/replay/locale regressions. |

| Purpose | Check lint declarations, discovery, rule behavior, report integrity, adapter confinement and native remediation/cancellation regressions without running the separate pipeline live fixture. |
| Scope | Runs nine ordered Node commands: stage, package boundary, adapter boundary, discovery, registry lifecycle, ESLint discipline, ESLint type evidence, report contract and remediation. This focused selection still executes actual native tools; it is not a static-only check and does not run test:live. The complete selected npm script declarations appear in the read-only definition below. Null means no declared hook, not a generic no-effect guarantee. Execution place: Invoke from repository root; npm --prefix selects the named package as script cwd. Relative selected paths are package-relative. |
| Environment and execution place | Use the prepared Node24/npm checkout with locked workspace dependencies. npm supplies node_modules/.bin for installed ESLint and TypeScript. Require Git, /bin/sleep, executable temporary files, symlink support, Linux /proc and process-group signalling for the remediation cases. No selected focused command requires shellcheck/shfmt merely because the separate live command does. Inherited PATH/Git configuration can affect native subprocesses. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Creates temporary policies, repositories, symlinks, local Git commits and real ESLint/tsc processes. Two ESLint suites create transient directories inside package src; the report suite writes then removes src/report-contract-hostile-fixture.json. Remediation executes sleeps, output overflow, Git smudge and TERM-resistant descendants, then timeout/abort/shutdown signalling. Selected finally blocks remove fixtures and restore GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL; interruption or cleanup failure can retain partial state. No cluster or remote model is selected. |
| Expected result and limits | Every &&-joined command must exit zero and Node remediation TAP must have no failed subtests. The report-contract JSON must name hostileCases:8 and cleanup:true. Expected findings/errors/cancellation are asserted negatives, not a clean-source result. A nonzero command stops the focused chain and must not be hidden by later output; successful focus does not establish the separate live stage or deployed activation. |
| Owner | [Lint maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#run-lint-for-a-selected-source-change); [Selected source-component maintainer](../extend/developer-handbook.md#route-each-source-change-to-its-documentation-owner); [plugin Foundation/SDK maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-sdk-or-shared-contracts) |
| When this changes | After lint policy/tool/discovery/path/report/timeout/cancellation changes, run this exact focused form and the affected regression. Add hostile identity/counter cases before changing the report version. Run the separate package build for static types and the separately selected live fixture only with its own native prerequisites. |

| Purpose | Check Studio adapter/preview contract assertions and the selected actual Chromium UI and asset/error interactions. |
| Scope | Runs studio-adapter Node tests, then Playwright with studio/playwright.config.mjs. The config selects every test under studio/tests, including studio.spec.mjs and remediation.spec.mjs, across desktop/phone/tablet projects. Desktop/mobile cases have explicit project-dependent skips. This standalone test does NOT run build:studio or prebuild, unlike the root verify:prism:studio compound. The complete selected npm script declarations appear in the read-only definition below. Null means no declared hook, not a generic no-effect guarantee. Execution place: Invoke from repository root; npm --prefix selects the named package as script cwd. Relative selected paths are package-relative. |
| Environment and execution place | Use locked Node24/npm, @playwright/test and Chromium/native browser libraries. Main config uses its fixed /ms-playwright Chromium headless-shell path if present, otherwise the installed Playwright browser. Identify the server on 127.0.0.1:4190: Playwright may reuse it or launch npm run dev:studio. Prepare the actual current dist-studio separately because selected remediation tests serve that bundle. Require writable Playwright output/temp directories, loopback ports and artifact link/fsync support. No live Control/PostgreSQL/OpenClaw/model or cluster is supplied by the local fixtures. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Reads Studio source/CSS/fixtures for Node assertions, launches browser processes/contexts and possibly a Vite development server, or reuses an existing server it does not own. Writes test-runner outputs and may write Vite cache state. Included remediation beforeAll creates temporary artifact storage and an ephemeral local HTTP server serving actual dist-studio and synthetic session/document endpoints; afterAll closes that server and removes its owned storage. Runner-managed browser/server cleanup is not an aggregate rollback; reused servers and build artifacts remain. |
| Expected result and limits | Both Node and Playwright phases must exit zero. Retain the real pass/fail/declared project-skip summary; declared desktop/mobile skips are not missing-tool skips. UI changes, stale/missing dist, wrong/reused server content, unavailable browser or fixture errors are failed observations. Zero proves only the selected local assertions, not production Control authentication or deployed Studio acceptance. |
| Owner | [Prism maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-prism-contracts-services-data-or-engine); [Selected source-component maintainer](../extend/developer-handbook.md#route-each-source-change-to-its-documentation-owner) |
| When this changes | After Studio adapter, preview, UI/navigation or asset behavior changes, build the intended bundle separately where required, then run this exact standalone test. Review both selected spec files and explicit project skips. Keep server identity and actual report; do not silently borrow a build result from the root compound or count a reused server as newly launched. |

### route-88: npm test --prefix tools/ops-mcp

Follow the [complete guide procedure](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-ops-mcp).

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Check Ops MCP authentication, local HTTP/TLS transport, Kubernetes read limits, Hubble diagnostic handling and bootstrap command routing without contacting a real cluster. |
| Scope | The package selects seven test/*.test.mjs files: authentication, bootstrap, diagnostics, http, hubble, kubernetes and local. Tests use actual spawned local MCP servers and HTTP/TLS sockets, injected executable Hubble output programs, and a migration script whose kubectl and python3 commands are replaced by owned call-logging fixtures. The separate policy_contract_test.py is not selected. These tests do not establish real cluster/RBAC, Hubble relay, external MCP connection or production readiness. The complete selected npm script declarations appear in the read-only definition below. No declared pretest/posttest hook. |
| Environment and execution place | Run from the prepared repository root as npm test --prefix tools/ops-mcp; npm selects tools/ops-mcp cwd and the independent package dependencies/lockfile. Use the documented Node24/npm host (package minimum Node22), installed @modelcontextprotocol/node and server, Hono and Zod dependencies, writable executable temporary storage and loopback HTTP/TLS ports. Require real OpenSSL req supporting -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days -keyout -out -subj and -addext, plus Bash, /usr/bin/env and Node on PATH for generated fixtures. No real kubectl, python3, Hubble binary, cluster token or production certificate is needed by the selected replacement/absent-token fixtures. Child servers inherit caller environment except explicit overrides/deletions; conflicting inherited Ops authentication, namespace, origin or TLS settings can fail setup and are not a supported skip. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Creates temporary bearer/token rotation files, self-signed private keys/certificates, fake executable Hubble/kubectl/python3 programs and migration call logs. Spawns native Node MCP server children on 127.0.0.1 with port0, actual OpenSSL children, actual Bash migration and owned Node Hubble fixture children; sends real local HTTP/TLS/MCP traffic. Credential-unavailable get_pod stops at its explicitly absent token file. Hubble tests force their own binary, including output-limit/nonzero/timeout children. Migration apply/cleanup goes only to the fake PATH-selected loggers; it does not invoke the real kubectl API. t.after/finally remove owned roots and stop children/servers; some child cleanup signals SIGTERM without awaiting exit. Setup/cleanup failure or interruption can leave processes/files, and no aggregate rollback is promised. |
| Expected result and limits | Node --test must exit zero with all seven files completing their selected assertions; preserve the actual TAP failures, setup errors and child diagnostics. Absent/weak bearer must refuse listening, rotation and namespace rejection must remain explicit, the unavailable Kubernetes read must report an error while tools/list and health remain usable, local TLS must reject wrong host/CA/redirect/oversize/timeout, and Hubble lost/partial/nonzero/byte-limit/timeout observations must not become complete success. Bootstrap logs must show the custom namespace route. Zero is this package-local contract result, not real cluster or external tool readiness. |
| Owner | [Ops MCP maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-ops-mcp); [Selected source-component maintainer](../extend/developer-handbook.md#route-each-source-change-to-its-documentation-owner) |
| When this changes | After changing Ops server/config/authentication, Kubernetes transport, diagnostic/Hubble handling, package scripts or bootstrap routing, run this exact package test with its separate locked dependencies and OpenSSL preflight. Update the matching negative fixture and keep namespace/credential boundaries. Run the separately documented policy/image/live checks only for their actual changed responsibilities; do not count the Python policy test or image acceptance as part of this npm command. |

  "pretest": null,

  "posttest": null
}

## Deployment Front Doors

All 41 public deployment forms are listed. Select the intended context and namespace before a cluster-affecting command.

### deploy-1: ./scripts/deploy.sh render &lt;nova&#124;buster&gt; [image&#124;code]

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Render the selected release without applying it; image is the default mode. Requires the selected runtime release. |
| Scope | Selected render/deployment/inspection procedure; exact entry and receiver ranges are in sourceEvidence.  |
| Environment and execution place | Local control host with Helm and the selected runtime release. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Read release/base/private values, write transient overrides/context files, and print Helm output; do not apply resources. |
| Expected result and limits | Rendered YAML follows selected image/bundle validation. Render-only returns before trust/cluster checks; code mode also skips URL preflight. This is not admission or availability proof. |
| Owner | [platform deployment maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-charts-or-gitops) |
| When this changes | When changing this entry, its defaults, values/Secret policy, or delegated receiver, update the CLI/reference meaning and check the affected render/contract receiver. For live procedures, use the intended context and required authority; inspect original job/resource/receipt outcomes before retrying uncertain effects. |

### deploy-2: ./scripts/deploy.sh render prism

| Responsibility | Contract |

| Purpose | Render the dedicated Prism release without applying it. Requires the selected runtime release. |

### ci-1: .github/workflows/auto-promote-runtime.yaml

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Select a compatible verified runtime and code release after an eligible main-branch build. |
| Scope | Automatic main-branch release selection and GitOps update; not a new image build. |
| Environment and execution place | GitHub runner with Node 24, Helm 3.18.4, GITOPS_ENABLED=true, contents-write/actions-read token, and serialized non-cancelling execution. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Fetch source-attempt receipts and releases; update release and GitOps files, commit, and push main. Argo can deploy the resulting selection. Concurrent push failure is not automatically rebased. |
| Expected result and limits | A selected=true result must be followed by validation and a successful push. Stale input, unchanged input, or an existing selection can return zero without a new deployment. |
| Owner | [Release/deployment maintainer](../extend/developer-handbook.md#route-each-source-change-to-its-documentation-owner) |
| When this changes | Change runtime-input detection, receipt eligibility, selection materialization, or GitOps output together; check selected source attempt, immutable digests, generated files, and production selection. |

### ci-5: .github/workflows/docs-checks.yaml

| Responsibility | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Validate documentation separately from trusted main-branch regeneration. |
| Scope | Untrusted validation and trusted update jobs have different credentials and output permissions. Both actual platform inventory generation/check delegates now include typed store-policy source/caller bindings; trusted regeneration does not imply policy approval. Platform policy acquisition also uses the existing selected native Helm/static resources and one separate policy-only Prism ingestion comparison, labelled helm:prism-ingestion-policy: ingestion.enabled is enabled with a typed boolean override, explicit render-only CPU/memory sizing and the existing native-worker fixture settings. The maintained selected Prism profile still disables ingestion. This comparison supplies only policy selection and is never merged into the original selected resource/signal/endpoint arrays; it is not a deployment, inferred default or observed capacity. |
| Environment and execution place | GitHub runner with Node 24, Go 1.26.3, Helm 3.22.0, checksum-verified Kubeconform, and Playwright; validation uses a read-only token, update uses contents-write. The platform producer uses an existing inventory sourceRevision before the shared-lock fallback and checks cited producer/authority bytes; this workflow does not pass its optional explicit --revision flag. A stale own-inventory source identity is therefore a STOP, not permission to claim HEAD was selected. The selected static PostgreSQL renderer also requires tar and a private writable OS temporary chart cache. A matching cached archive is reverified; a cache miss requires curl and HTTPS access to the locked chart transport (the selected PostgreSQL lock uses immutable Docker Hub OCI manifest/layer acquisition; supported HTTPS archive locks use direct HTTPS). Node parses Go source statically; these direct platform commands do not invoke a Go binary. Other aggregate/CI delegates retain their separately declared Go/tool prerequisites. Native source custody and normal publication require distinct preparation states. The supported maintenance sequence is clean committed Source and native platform generation/check first, then npm run sync-contract --prefix skills/common/plugins/openclaw-agent-observer to prepare publication runtime imports from the same committed contracts/agent-observability/v1/src. This original sync removes/recreates only its ignored src/generated/agent-observability target and copies canonical files; verify exact canonical file set/bytes. It is not an automatic hook of this platform command. Before any later clean native check, remove only an unchanged verified-owned generated copy after its consumers have stopped; never remove canonical Source or unrelated data. Separate staged successes do not establish simultaneous filesystem compatibility or successful execution of a containing docs:check/docs:publish-check/CI pipeline. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Validation installs tools, regenerates local files, tests, builds HTML, and rejects unexpected differences. Trusted main can update the SourceLock, regenerate, commit, and push only the allowed outputs. The platform child itself does not advance the shared lock or execute runtime stores, SQL, backup or cleanup; the separate trusted docs generator retains its existing SourceLock-write authority. Existing tool installation, browser/network acquisition, generated writes, commit/push and output-allowset boundaries remain. The selected local child-renderer closure includes LiteLLM configuration rendering and PostgreSQL recovery-manifest rendering; its imported volume preflight is not called because this producer does not pass --preflight. PostgreSQL service selection stages a versions.json-pinned chart in os.tmpdir()/kubeclaw-infrastructure-charts-<uid>, requiring a real owner-private directory. Existing archives are size/SHA/name/version/appVersion checked with tar; absent archives trigger curl HTTPS/OCI acquisition, bounded manifest/layer/digest checks and archive verification before rename into the retained cache. Helm performs an offline template/upgrade-view render with the local image post-renderer; the render-only password marker must not escape into resources, and reserved images must match pinned versions. It does not run PostgreSQL, backup SQL/shell or kubectl. Owned download-* directories are removed in finally; the private cache and verified archive remain, including after a later producer/check/mutation failure. Bad existing cache/archive, missing tools, network/acquisition, digest, archive identity, image or rendering failures stop; no automatic bad-cache repair or whole-cache rollback is promised. Thus --check compares normal outputs without writing them but is not filesystem-readonly or necessarily network-free. Repeated mutation calls can reuse/populate this separate cache; removing the owned mutation/Git fixture does not remove it. The rendered-policy helper receives these already acquired resources without starting tools or runtime owners. It selects one exact source/origin/kind/name/namespace, requires own-field paths and declared nested identities, and parses embedded registry ConfigMap YAML only as one valid unique-key/no-alias document. Missing/ambiguous resources or fields and identity changes stop. Values retain selected native resource provenance, conditional/fixture limits and outer Source authentication; declaration location is not misrepresented as selected-field offset. Original templates are not executed as arbitrary JavaScript or reimplemented by a scanner. The delegated platform producer performs the policy-only comparison Helm render described in Scope; normal child chart-cache/tool/network and failure effects already described remain in force. This adds no contract synchronization or runtime cleanup automatically. |
| Expected result and limits | Validation is not filesystem read-only. Output guards reject changes outside the allowset; existing source/purpose qualification failures still fail. |
| Owner | [documentation](../extend/documentation-maintenance.md) |
| When this changes | Check generation, source-first qualification, native publication, trust separation, and output-allowset guards when changing either job or its receivers. Changes to producer revision/custody, either policy helper, supported selectors, actual store source/caller/default/cleanup authority, guidance family meaning/binding, selected template values, qualified contexts, explanation anchor or map identity require this exact producer/check plus its native policy source/custody tests and declared platform drift matrix. Inspect exact Source-derived values versus fallbacks/effective unknowns, refusal diagnostics, owned-fixture restoration and a meaningful reader cleanup/STOP decision; obtain independent affected-topic review. Commit actual Source before explicit current-revision generation; preserve the shared lock and unrelated outputs. Do not refresh mappings/baselines to conceal mismatch. Changes to conditional render recipe, selected origin/resource/nested identity, embedded YAML grammar or public provenance labels require the focused rendered-policy source tests plus the real native Job-TTL, embedded-registry and conditional-quarantine value projection/refusal/restoration controls. Preserve selected-profile absence and original surface arrays. Run original normal publication only after canonical contract synchronization; retain actual failed publication diagnostics until a genuine successful current successor exists. |

| Responsibility | Contract |

| Scope | Eight retention cases, an unknown-column negative control, and fixture cleanup against the prepared native schema. |

| When this changes | Change the SQL, native schema/preparer, fixture, negative control, restoration, and cleanup checks together. |

| Scope | Local/native process, service, browser, security, and PostgreSQL fixture jobs; not a production deployment. |
| Environment and execution place | PR or reusable main-build GitHub runner with Node 24, Docker, systemd scope, nginx, Redis, PostgreSQL 17, Playwright, Trivy, and installed native tools. |
| Authority, writes and remaining state | Build sandbox/packages; start temporary services/databases; write artifacts/caches; install host packages and adjust AppArmor. Individual job failures can coexist under non-cancelled dependency guards. |
| Expected result and limits | Required job status must succeed. Four shards are a partition, not a count of all tests; fixture success is not whole-production acceptance. |
| Owner | [Nova Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-nova-lifecycle-scheduling-or-run-authority); [Worker Core maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-worker-core-or-native-execution); [Buster maintainers for execution; Nova maintainers for final import](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-buster-plans-providers-or-result-import); [Prism maintainers](../extend/developer-handbook.md#change-prism-contracts-services-data-or-engine) |
| When this changes | Change test partitioning, reliability groups, actual receivers, and host/service prerequisites together; inspect required-job dependencies and failure reporting. |
